Mesuré sur **104 sondes** : entre 84 % et 100 % des analyses d'une simple demande d'image. La normalisation se fait désormais à l'entrée du parsing, une fois, plutôt qu'à chaque lecture — ce qui supprime au passage un journal affirmant avoir effacé une compétence jamais détectée.
- **Un nom de compétence inexistant pilotait le tour entier** — le routeur donne à ce champ une priorité absolue. En juillet, un nom halluciné n'avait atterri sur le bon chemin que **par accident**, parce qu'aucune compétence ne le portait. L'existence est maintenant vérifiée dans la portée du compte, avec repli permissif tant que le catalogue n'est pas chargé : un catalogue vide signifie « au démarrage », pas « aucune compétence ».
- **Une réponse terminée restait invisible sur téléphone** — le serveur enregistrait bien la réponse, mais le client ne quittait jamais l'état « en cours », donc ne tentait jamais de se rattacher au tour resté vivant en arrière-plan. Sur toute la période observée, **aucun** appel de reprise n'a été émis.

### Tests

- **Chaque garde a été falsifiée avant d'être conservée** : vignette retirée puis vignette modifiée d'un seul octet, volume absent du fichier de construction, et — pour la plus importante — la régression exacte que le cumul redoute, injectée dans le nœud de réponse pour vérifier qu'un seul test tombe.
- **Trois nouvelles gardes** : tout volume nommé doit être créé par l'image qui le monte, toute compétence doit livrer son aperçu et celui-ci doit correspondre à son générateur, et le contrat de sortie de l'analyseur est vérifié à la frontière.
- **Le plafond de taille de fichier a mordu** pendant le chantier : plutôt que de le relever, le contrat de sortie de l'analyseur est devenu un module à part et le plafond est **descendu** de 1 142 à 1 020.

## [1.25.24] - 2026-07-27

**Le produit était utilisable, mais pas toujours trouvable.** Sur un téléphone, sous 768 px, la barre de navigation disparaissait et rien ne la remplaçait : depuis le chat, les réglages et l'aide n'étaient atteignables qu'en tapant une URL. La checklist de démarrage pointait **six de ses sept entrées** vers la page de réglages nue — « choisir une personnalité » déposait l'utilisateur en haut de trente accordéons fermés. Sept des neuf cartes de l'accueil **ne rendent rien du tout** quand leur source n'est pas configurée : un compte neuf découvrait deux cartes vides et sept trous invisibles. Les quotas n'avertissaient jamais : rien, rien, rien, puis un mur, en pleine tâche. Les images générées étaient supprimées au bout d'un délai sans jamais le dire. Un tour en échec était un cul-de-sac : il fallait retrouver sa question et la retaper. Et en allemand à 768 px, le bouton de déconnexion se trouvait **235 px hors de l'écran**, rogné par un `overflow-x: hidden` qui faisait mesurer zéro à toutes les gardes de débordement existantes. Cette version est cette passe-là. Tests backend **15 877 → 15 954** (842 fichiers), frontend **2 832 → 3 460**, **97/97** parcours navigateur hermétiques, plafond de complexité backend **abaissé** (89 → 87).

### Added

- **Le logo devient la navigation sur téléphone** — sous `md`, il ouvre un menu vers les quatre destinations du bandeau au lieu d'être un lien « accueil » sans issue. Deux éléments exclusifs plutôt qu'un élément qui change de rôle : un lien à une largeur et un bouton à une autre ne peut annoncer ni l'un ni l'autre à une technologie d'assistance. La cible tactile passe à 44 px, la barre n'ayant pas la largeur d'un menu hamburger supplémentaire.
- **Dix-sept sections de réglages adressables** (`?section=…`) — la table est la source unique des cibles, et chaque entrée est vérifiée contre le composant qui la déclare : le fichier doit exister, déclarer la valeur d'accordéon annoncée, **et être rendu dans l'onglet que la table revendique**. Auparavant deux jetons seulement étaient compris.
- **Les cartes non configurées sont nommées** — une seule ligne discrète, chaque nom de carte pointant vers la section qui la configure. Jamais sept cartes promotionnelles : sur mobile la grille est déjà tout l'écran. Les cartes que l'utilisateur a lui-même masquées ne sont jamais mentionnées.
- **Avertissement de quota avant le mur** — le backend calculait déjà un état gradué (`warning` à 80 %, `critical` à 95 %) et six dimensions ; le chat n'en lisait que deux champs booléens. La dimension annoncée est la **contraignante** (le pourcentage le plus haut, puisque n'importe laquelle bloque le compte), et la date de réinitialisation n'est promise que pour une limite de cycle — une limite absolue ne se réinitialise pas.
- **Les images générées annoncent leur échéance** — la date vient du backend, jamais d'un « 24 h » écrit en dur : le TTL est configurable, une constante dans l'interface finirait par mentir. Un message sans échéance (historique antérieur) ne dit rien plutôt que de deviner.
- **Rejouer un tour en échec** — la bulle d'erreur épingle la question qui l'a produite, et le bouton rejoue **exactement** celle-là, pas le dernier texte utilisateur au moment du clic (une notification proactive peut s'être glissée entre les deux).
- **375 exemples de FAQ cliquables** dans les 6 langues — les phrases à puce déjà rédigées deviennent des boutons qui préremplissent la zone de saisie. Le HTML environnant garde son chemin de rendu, chaque commande devient un vrai `<button>` dont le texte est échappé par React : la posture XSS est strictement inchangée.
- **Trois amorces sur un chat vide**, choisies parce qu'elles aboutissent sur n'importe quel compte — sans connecteur, sans mémoire, sans historique.
- **Suivi des appels téléphoniques** — l'endpoint `GET /telephony/calls` existait depuis la livraison du domaine et n'était consommé par rien. Une section dédiée dans les réglages, et un bandeau pendant l'appel : le produit devenait totalement muet entre la confirmation et le compte rendu.
- **Neuf confirmations natives remplacées** — les actions les plus irréversibles du produit (supprimer un utilisateur, l'**effacer**, réécrire une table tarifaire) passaient par `window.confirm()`, qui ignore le thème, prend ses libellés au système d'exploitation et bloque le fil principal. La fermeture par Échap ou par clic extérieur vaut refus, jamais consentement.
- **Doctrine de visibilité mobile, rendue opposable** — une table déclare, pour chaque surface conditionnée à la largeur, si elle est bloquante, substituée ou réservée au bureau, avec sa raison écrite. Les tests la tiennent contre le code : chaque emplacement doit exister, porter la variante Tailwind du seuil annoncé, et une surface coûteuse doit être **montée conditionnellement**, pas simplement masquée en CSS — `display:none` monte quand même le composant, qui continue de requêter et de consommer la batterie.
- **Règle de priorité unique pour la bande sous le fil de conversation** — mesuré : une carte d'approbation en attente plus des suggestions de suivi occupaient 443 px d'une coquille de 716 px. Mais la hauteur n'est que le symptôme : LIA ne peut pas demander une confirmation *et* proposer trois questions sans rapport au-dessus. L'arbitrage porte sur le sens, jamais sur des pixels — supprimer un bloc parce que la fenêtre est courte finirait par masquer un mur de quota sans explication.
- **Cliquet sur la troncature des traductions** ([ADR-158](docs/architecture/ADR-158-Locale-Content-Truncation-Ratchet.md)) — la parité de clés ne mesure pas ce qu'il y a derrière la clé : une locale qui remplace une réponse de 500 caractères par un résumé de 150 passait indéfiniment.
- **Atteignabilité des quatre thèmes du journal** ([ADR-159](docs/architecture/ADR-159-Journal-Theme-Reachability.md)) — deux des quatre thèmes n'avaient **aucune** entrée en base, en dev comme en production.

### Changed

- **Le validateur sémantique ne demande plus deux fois la même confirmation.** Il s'arrêtait sur « action irréversible » pour des actions qui portent déjà leur propre confirmation en aval — les dix-neuf types de brouillon montrent un aperçu et attendent un accord explicite avant d'exécuter. L'utilisateur devait **insister** pour être obéi. Le jugement porte désormais sur la structure du plan, jamais sur le caractère consécutif ressenti de l'action.
- **Le titre par défaut d'une conversation est localisé** dans les 6 langues, chacune avec sa convention de date (`26/07` en France, `07/26` aux États-Unis, `26.07` en Allemagne, `年月日` en Chine) — une seule forme se lirait comme une date fausse dans la moitié des langues.
- **La coquille du chat est dimensionnée sur la fenêtre dynamique** (`dvh`) — `100vh` est la hauteur qu'aurait la page si la barre d'adresse du navigateur était rétractée, c'est-à-dire pas l'état dans lequel une page se charge sur mobile : le bas du conteneur, donc la zone de saisie, se trouvait sous la ligne de flottaison. Un test interdit désormais toute contrainte de hauteur en `vh` seul.
- **Les avis de connecteur se condensent** quand ils partagent la même action — un jeton Google expiré invalide Gmail, Agenda et Drive d'un coup, soit trois lignes ambrées. Des actions différentes restent listées en entier : aucune phrase unique ne serait vraie des deux.
- **`brace-expansion` corrigé par un patch d'interopérabilité** ([ADR-157](docs/architecture/ADR-157-Patched-Brace-Expansion.md)) plutôt que par une exemption d'audit — l'alerte haute n'avait aucune version corrigée compatible avec la chaîne de linters.
- **Neuf modules frontend orphelins supprimés** ([ADR-156](docs/architecture/ADR-156-Removal-Of-Nine-Orphan-Frontend-Modules.md)) — 1 561 lignes de code et 592 de tests, dont **deux composants déjà cassés** : ils interrogeaient des clés i18n absentes des six locales, donc montés ils auraient affiché des identifiants bruts.
- **L'historique d'appels n'est plus rendu deux fois** — la nouvelle section et l'ancien encart du bloc connecteur affichaient les mêmes lignes sur la même page, et demandaient deux fois la même requête.

### Fixed

- **Un appel téléphonique refusé bloquait tous les suivants pendant quinze minutes.** Le fournisseur répond **HTTP 200 même lorsqu'il refuse de composer** (numéro émetteur non vérifié, crédit épuisé) : le refus est dans le corps, sous `success: false`. Ignoré, il laissait une ligne en `DIALING` que rien ne terminerait jamais — et, sans identifiant de conversation, une ligne que la sonde d'auto-réparation ne peut même pas interroger. Le message rendu distingue désormais le transitoire (« réessaie dans un instant ») du refus de configuration, où réessayer ne changerait rien.
- **La déconnexion était hors de l'écran sur tablette.** Entre 768 px et 1024 px le bandeau montrait simultanément la navigation et les libellés des contrôles ; en allemand, le bouton de déconnexion débordait de 235 px. Rien ne l'avait vu parce que `html { overflow-x: hidden }` rogne le débordement au lieu de produire un défilement : la garde de reflow existante mesurait **zéro sur 108 échantillons**. La nouvelle garde compare chaque contrôle à la fenêtre, par largeur et par langue.
- **La zone de saisie n'était pas alignée** — un `<textarea>` est un élément *inline* : sa ligne de base ajoutait 6 px sous lui, si bien que son conteneur mesurait 54 px quand les trois contrôles voisins en faisaient 48. Mesuré en navigateur, pas assuré par une classe CSS.
- **L'indicateur d'espaces RAG était collé au bord droit** et pouvait recouvrir le badge d'écoute active ; les deux partagent désormais une rangée centrée, ce qui rend le chevauchement impossible par construction. Sous 640 px son nom accessible se réduisait au chiffre : un lecteur d'écran annonçait « 2 ».
- **Le titre de conversation restait français** pour tout le monde : la table localisée et le service étaient corrects, mais **un seul des quatre appelants** transmettait la langue — et pas celui du chat. Une garde AST refuse désormais tout appelant qui n'énonce pas la sienne.
- **Le second type de métadonnées de fin de flux avait pris du retard** — la même forme était réécrite à la main en six endroits, et la copie portée par l'action SSE ignorait le champ d'échéance ajouté ailleurs. Une déclaration unique remplace les six.
- **Le type des jetons de réglages ne protégeait rien** : déclaré sur un `Record<string, …>`, `keyof` s'effondrait en `string`, si bien qu'un lien profond mal orthographié compilait proprement jusqu'au lien mort. Corrigé par `satisfies` et une garde de type — le compilateur a immédiatement trouvé une erreur réelle dans les tests existants.
- **Une constante de planificateur orpheline** subsistait d'un contournement retiré, un test reconstruisait une table par expression régulière sur le code source au lieu de l'importer, et un commentaire justifiait une écriture par un comportement de session que le projet n'a pas.
- **Deux régressions de cliquet dans le travail livré** : un fichier passait de 1 051 à 1 061 SLOC pour un plafond de 1 052, et `initiate_call` franchissait le seuil de complexité. Corrigées par extraction — un sérialiseur partagé et l'interprétation de la réponse du fournisseur — jamais en relevant un plafond.
- **Quatre renvois de documentation** pointaient encore vers des modules supprimés.

### Tests

- **97 parcours navigateur hermétiques verts** sur un build de production servi dans le conteneur, serveur vérifié vivant avant et après la suite. Onze nouveaux fichiers e2e : accessibilité du bandeau par largeur **et par langue**, navigation mobile, substituts mobiles, liens profonds de réglages, avertissement de quota, alignement de la zone de saisie mesuré en pixels.
- **Frontend 2 832 → 3 460 tests** (296 fichiers), backend **15 877 → 15 954** (842 fichiers).
- **Une garde de placement des clés i18n** — la parité compare des ensembles de clés et reste aveugle à un bloc inséré dans la mauvaise section de la même façon dans les six locales : la parité passe pendant que l'écran affiche `usage_limits.warning.warning`. C'est arrivé pendant ce chantier, et seule une exécution en navigateur l'a montré.
- Chaque garde ajoutée a été **falsifiée** avant d'être conservée : on casse volontairement ce qu'elle protège et on vérifie qu'elle rougit.

## [1.25.23] - 2026-07-26

**Les tests qui ne tournaient pas — et les défauts qu'ils cachaient.** Dix fichiers de test portaient un `skipif` sur `OPENAI_API_KEY` au niveau module : **219 tests n'avaient jamais été exécutés**, sur le classifieur HITL, la reprise après approbation, l'exécuteur de brouillons et la construction du graphe. Un test sauté est vert, rien ne le signale. Réactivés, **142 revenaient au rouge** (125 échecs, 17 erreurs) contre 92 verts — écrits contre une API migrée depuis. Les réparer a exhumé des défauts bien réels : la voix coupait **tous les nombres en deux** (« il fait trois. » puis, dans un autre extrait audio, « cinq degrés »), un rappel était **perdu définitivement** si l'utilisateur atteignait sa limite d'usage à la minute du déclenchement, un utilisateur chinois recevait ses notifications en anglais, et la valeur qu'un utilisateur venait de corriger dans une confirmation disparaissait de la conversation pour tous les outils sauf un. Le job CI « agents » passe de **978 à 1 158 tests exécutés, zéro sauté**. Tests backend **15 331 → 15 877** (837 fichiers), frontend **2 729 → 2 832**, plancher de couverture **61 % → 62 %**.

### Added

- **Taxonomie d'action HITL** ([ADR-153](docs/architecture/ADR-153-HITL-Action-Taxonomy.md)) — le type annoncé au classifieur est désormais dérivé du **verbe** du nom d'outil, avec un repli par sous-chaîne ordonné destructif d'abord et sans aucun nom de domaine. Une assertion au démarrage refuse de booter si un type d'action peut être annoncé sans bloc d'exemples derrière lui : un repli silencieux sur le bloc générique est exactement ainsi qu'un classifieur cesse d'être contextuel sans que personne ne le voie.
- **`HitlResumeMessage` — les avis de reprise dans les 6 langues.** Trois phrases françaises codées en dur étaient diffusées **mot pour mot** à l'utilisateur lorsqu'un brouillon lui était représenté pour précision. La localisation est placée là où la langue est connue : le classifieur n'invente plus de question, il ne connaît pas la langue de l'utilisateur.
- **Points cardinaux du vent traduits** — une source unique renvoyant un code, résolu en 6 langues côté serveur comme côté client. Les deux tables qui coexistaient épelaient l'une en anglais, l'autre en français : la même mesure se lisait différemment selon la carte.
- **Trois blocs d'exemples few-shot** (`transfert`, `réponse`, `modification`) — une réponse à un e-mail n'a pas de destinataire, et les exemples d'envoi poussaient le modèle à proposer un paramètre que l'outil ne peut pas accepter.
- **Cinq gardes exécutables** : aucun module de test ne peut se désactiver en silence sur une clé de provider absente ([ADR-155](docs/architecture/ADR-155-No-Env-Skipped-Test-Suite.md)) ; aucun appel `fetch` brut ne peut réapparaître hors d'une liste justifiée ; aucun test ne peut fabriquer la forme d'erreur d'une bibliothèque que le projet n'utilise pas ; la partition des domaines filtrables en opération de série est vérifiée au démarrage ; et une section de FAQ ne peut plus déclarer un nombre de questions différent de celles réellement écrites — la boucle de rendu est bornée par ce compteur, si bien qu'une question ajoutée sans lui **ne s'affiche jamais**, dans les 6 langues et sans qu'aucun contrôle existant ne le voie.

### Changed

- **Frontière de phrase pour la synthèse vocale** ([ADR-154](docs/architecture/ADR-154-TTS-Sentence-Boundaries.md)) — un délimiteur ne ferme une phrase qu'en fin d'entrée ou suivi d'une espace. Un point collé au caractère suivant appartient au token, pas à la prose. Les deux découpeurs du pipeline vocal sont désormais épinglés par une table de cas partagée et par un test qui exige leur accord.
- **Les messages d'erreur du serveur atteignent l'utilisateur.** Vingt-et-un endroits lisaient la réponse sous la forme d'une bibliothèque que le projet n'utilise pas : tout détail renvoyé par l'API était remplacé par un texte générique. Un point de passage unique lit désormais l'enveloppe FastAPI sous ses trois formes, y compris la liste d'erreurs de validation qui s'affichait « [object Object] ».
- **`ProactiveMessages.notification_title` normalise la langue lui-même** — les appelants détiennent des locales brutes de toutes orthographes ; la sûreté ne doit pas dépendre de leur discipline.
- **Plancher de couverture backend porté à 62 %** (mesuré 64,1 %), les seuils frontend maintenus faute des deux points de marge exigés par la doctrine.
- **Code mort supprimé** : trois hooks frontend sans consommateur ([ADR-152](docs/architecture/ADR-152-Removal-Of-Orphan-Frontend-Hooks.md), 861 lignes), un filtre HITL dont le prédicat était `return False` en dur et dont l'option n'était passée par aucun appelant, et une table de 37 expressions régulières françaises qu'aucun chemin n'atteignait plus.

### Fixed

- **La voix coupait tous les nombres en deux.** Les deux découpeurs de phrases traitaient tout point comme une fin de phrase : « Il fait 3.5 degrés » était prononcé « il fait trois. » puis, **dans un extrait audio distinct**, « cinq degrés ». Idem pour les prix, les numéros de version et les URL. Sur le chemin progressif, le tampon grandit caractère par caractère : `"3."` y est un état transitoire parfaitement normal, et parler dessus revient à répondre avant d'avoir fini de lire.
- **Un rappel pouvait être perdu définitivement.** La sélection des rappels échus prend un bail en basculant la ligne en `PROCESSING`, et la requête suivante ne regarde que les `PENDING`. Deux sorties de boucle ne relâchaient pas ce bail : un utilisateur qui atteignait sa limite d'usage à la minute du déclenchement ne recevait jamais son rappel, sans erreur ni trace.
- **Un utilisateur chinois recevait ses notifications de rappel en anglais** — la table était indexée sur `zh` alors que la langue enregistrée est `zh-CN`. C'est la troisième occurrence de ce défaut ; la table centrale créée pour l'éliminer normalise désormais elle-même.
- **La correction saisie dans une confirmation disparaissait de la conversation.** La reformulation d'une modification était câblée sur un seul nom d'outil ; pour tous les autres elle produisait « exécute X avec les paramètres modifiés » — or ce message **remplace le tour de l'utilisateur** dans l'état, donc la valeur qu'il venait de donner n'existait plus.
- **Une suppression d'e-mail était annoncée au classifieur comme un envoi** — le nom de domaine « email » siégeait dans la branche du verbe « send », testée avant celle de « delete ». La règle de sûreté du prompt (sur une suppression, ne jamais approuver un doute) ne pouvait donc pas s'appliquer. Les outils de lecture d'e-mails étaient annoncés comme des envois pour la même raison.
- **Une réponse 5xx sans corps était traitée comme un succès** dans les deux clients HTTP : le retour anticipé sur corps vide précédait le contrôle de statut. L'appelant lisait un champ sur rien, ou affichait « aucune donnée » pour une panne.
- **Le panneau de personnalité ne survivait pas à une session expirée** — huit fonctions contournaient le client HTTP commun, donc ni redirection sur 401, ni délai d'expiration, et quatre lectures divergentes du message d'erreur.
- **Une confirmation de suppression de libellé ne nommait pas ce qu'elle supprimait** — le gabarit traduit existait dans les 6 langues, mais l'échelle de conditions n'avait pas de branche pour ce type.
- **Le filtrage d'une opération en série pouvait vider le registre ou abandonner un plan déjà confirmé** — les domaines dont l'identifiant est composite (itinéraires, positions, météo) régénéraient des identifiants introuvables.
- **La latitude 0 et la longitude 0 étaient perdues** — l'équateur et le méridien de Greenwich passaient pour des coordonnées absentes, et l'itinéraire retombait sur l'adresse textuelle.
- **Le taux de change était relu en base à chaque calcul de coût** — donc à chaque appel de modèle. La méthode estampillait le cache sans jamais y écrire la valeur, derrière un nom, une docstring et une machinerie d'invalidation qui décrivaient tous les trois un cache.
- **Un cap « N/A » s'affichait comme un vent de nord**, et une date de fin d'événement transmise sous une forme inattendue faisait disparaître toute la section agenda du briefing.

### Tests

- **219 tests réactivés** ([ADR-155](docs/architecture/ADR-155-No-Env-Skipped-Test-Suite.md)). Dix fichiers se désactivaient sur l'absence de clé de provider ; huit ont reçu un harnais hermétique (store LangGraph en mémoire, registre d'agents doublé, session TCM neutralisée), deux qui appellent réellement un modèle deux fois par test sont désormais marqués `e2e` — leur exclusion est **lisible dans la commande CI** au lieu d'être un silence. La liste d'exemption de la garde ADR-155 est vide ; en contrepartie la liste F006 (« aucun test ne tourne dans zéro job ») passe de 11 à 49 entrées — la dette ne grandit pas, elle **devient visible** : un test sauté sur clé absente restait collecté et sélectionné, donc compté comme couvert.
- L'invariant que six de ces tests protégeaient — le routeur écrit sa décision dans l'historique de routage, jamais dans la conversation — tient à la valeur de retour d'**une** fonction : il est désormais prouvé au niveau du nœud, en quelques millisecondes, sans piloter le graphe entier contre un vrai modèle.
- Chaque défaut a été **prouvé avant d'être corrigé** : la classification annoncée pour les 96 outils réellement enregistrés, le rappel laissé en `PROCESSING`, les phrases prononcées caractère par caractère pour reproduire le tampon qui se termine sur un point.
- Deux tests épinglaient un bug plutôt qu'un contrat : l'un exigeait qu'un message d'exception brut parte dans un prompt, l'autre exigeait le rappel statique de métriques qui **doublait le comptage des jetons**. Corrigés vers l'invariant réel, avec la raison écrite.

## [1.25.22] - 2026-07-25

**Second security wave — and a counter-audit of the first.** Three controls announced in v1.25.20 turned out not to exist. The rate-limit alert lived in a rule file Prometheus does not load *and* that `prepare_config.sh` regenerates from a template, so it could never fire and would have vanished at the next deploy. The deploy's permission hardening ended in a bare `echo PERMS_HARDENED` that runs whether or not a single `chmod` succeeded — a check that could not fail. And the global rate limit was bypassable by prefixing any request with `/health`. Each is now real, each is verified rather than announced, and each carries an executable guard so the class cannot return. The wave also closed defects the audit never listed: an IDOR on push-token revocation, an HSTS header the API emitted with `includeSubDomains; preload` against the project's own written policy, an email address that escaped the PII filter whenever it appeared in free text, and the frontend published on every network interface while the other fifteen ports were loopback-only. Backend tests **15,031 → 15,331**.

### Added

- **`GlobalRateLimitDegraded` alert, in the file Prometheus actually loads** (SEC-016) — the vital core goes 13 → 14. Threshold `ALERT_CORE_RATE_LIMIT_DEGRADED_RPS` (0.01 req/s over 5 minutes, same in every environment), a linked runbook, and two promtool cases: one proving it fires under a real outage, one proving a single Redis hiccup does *not* — which is what buys the threshold over a naive `> 0`.
- **Three executable guards closing the classes this wave exposed** — `test_alerts_core_guard.py` (the committed rule file must be its template's production render, every alert must link a runbook that exists and own a promtool case, the three threshold sets must declare the same keys); `test_compose_secret_scope_guard.py` (no service takes the full `.env` without a written reason, the web container receives no credential, every published port binds to loopback); and a deploy-driver case proving the hardening step refuses to continue on modes it did not obtain.
- **`navigateToAuthorizationUrl`** (SEC-002) — a single guarded entry point for the eight places that hand an API-supplied URL to `window.location`. A `javascript:` URL there does not navigate, it executes in the LIA origin. Defence in depth: the backend already validates MCP authorization endpoints, but the guard now protects the primitive rather than depending on every current and future endpoint remembering to.
- **`getExistingFcmToken`** — returns this device's push token without ever prompting, so logout can revoke it. `requestNotificationPermission` could not serve: it would pop a permission dialog at the exact moment someone signs out.
- **Frontend SBOM** (SEC-021) — the missing half of the inventory, built from `pnpm-lock.yaml` with the Trivy already in the pipeline (545 components, CycloneDX 1.7). Half an inventory answers "are we affected?" with "for Python, yes".
- Settings `TELEGRAM_UPDATE_DEDUP_TTL_SECONDS` (replay window for a Telegram `update_id`) and `HSTS_MAX_AGE` on the API side.

### Changed

- **HSTS is one ladder for both surfaces** (SEC-025) — the API hardcoded `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` while the web app served a staged `max-age` from `HSTS_MAX_AGE`, and both directives are excluded by the project's own documented policy because they are near-irreversible. Both now read the same variable; the production step moves to 2592000 (one month). Removing the directives does not retract pins browsers already hold — those expire on their own — it stops adding more.
- **Trivy is blocking** (SEC-021) — it reported into the Security tab and passed unconditionally, which makes a scanner a dashboard rather than a gate. Measured at 0 findings across every severity before flipping it. What it reads (the pip manifest, pnpm without dev dependencies) stays narrower than what ships, deliberately: pip-audit already gates the lockfile and pnpm audit already covers dev dependencies.
- **The web container no longer receives the production secret set** (SEC-037) — `env_file: .env` handed a Next.js process the database credentials, the Fernet key, the JWT secret and every LLM and OAuth secret, none of which it uses. Replaced by the measured runtime need; the rule for extending it is that anything non-secret may be added freely, and a secret means the frontend is doing something it should ask the API to do.
- **Permission hardening is verified and blocking** (SEC-013) — the deploy reads the resulting modes back with `stat` and refuses to reach `docker compose up` when the production `.env` is not 0600 inside a 0700 directory. Continuing past a failed hardening means knowingly starting the platform with its secrets readable.

### Fixed

- **The deploy script accepted a `RemoteDir` that erases the server** (SEC-038) — the value is interpolated into `sudo rm -rf ~/$RemoteDir/*`, and its denylist accepted `..` (every home directory on the host), `.ssh`, `lia foo` (two targets) and a trailing newline. Replaced by an anchored single-segment allowlist, validated once before the first interpolation rather than next to the destructive command — the backup step at the previous stage ran unguarded.
- **The global rate limit could be bypassed by prefixing a request** (SEC-016) — exemptions matched with `startswith`, so `/healthz` or `/metrics-flood` crossed the API unlimited. They answer 404, but a 404 still costs a full middleware traversal at whatever rate the client can produce. Exemptions are now exact; the same latent pattern was removed from the body-size middleware before its list is ever filled.
- **Anyone could revoke someone else's push notifications** — `unregister_token` deleted by token value with no ownership filter, while its sibling `delete_token_by_id` had always scoped its delete to the user. Found while wiring the endpoint for logout.
- **Signing out left the device receiving the account's notifications** (SEC-039) — the push token outlived the session, so on a shared computer the next person read them on the lock screen. Revoked before `/auth/logout`, because that endpoint needs the session the logout is about to destroy.
- **The Telegram webhook read the request body before checking the secret** (SEC-024), and processed a redelivered update twice — the agent answered twice and a `/start <code>` consumed the OTP a second time. The header is verified first (it is a shared secret, not an HMAC over the payload), and each `update_id` is claimed in Redis, failing open if Redis is down.
- **Position and geolocation consent survived a logout** (SEC-034) — both keys are global, so on a shared browser profile account B read where account A was, and kept collecting position under a consent B never gave.
- **Chat images leaked the conversation URL** (SEC-027) — every image in the Markdown render path, and its JavaScript preload, now sends `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`. Image sources are frequently third-party and often attacker-influenced.
- **An email address in free log text escaped the PII filter** (SEC-012) — the `event` field bypasses the full sanitizer to avoid mangling event names; the bypass now also pseudonymizes addresses, a shape no snake_case event name can contain.
- **The frontend was published on every network interface** (SEC-015) — reachable from the LAN without passing through Cloudflare, so without the WAF, the TLS termination or the access logs. It was the single exception among sixteen published ports.
- A Telegram payload that is valid JSON but not an object (`[]`, `null`, a number) raised inside the request handler and answered 500 — and a 500 is exactly what makes Telegram redeliver the same payload forever. Found in counter-review of this wave's own work.

### Tests

- **Backend 15,031 → 15,331**, frontend 2,567 → 2,729, deploy driver 47 → 50 Pester cases, plus two promtool cases on the new alert. The jump includes a parallel quality effort that landed in the same release: pure-helper extractions across the orchestrator, routes and briefing formatters, and a shared `api-error` module that gives the connector hooks and Server Actions one place to read FastAPI's error envelope.
- Every fix was **falsified**: the previous behaviour was restored and the test verified to fail. The old `RemoteDir` rule accepted 8 of 14 hostile values; a `> 0` alert threshold fires on the Redis hiccup the new one ignores; the `startswith` exemption let all 8 bypass paths through.
- The permission-hardening command was executed against a real POSIX filesystem (`644/755` → `600/700`) after Git Bash on NTFS reported a false failure — `chmod` does not apply there, which would have made the new blocking check look broken.

## [1.25.21] - 2026-07-25

**Generational RAG continuity** ([ADR-150](docs/architecture/ADR-150-RAG-Generational-Continuity.md)). Reindexing a space used to re-embed every document and drop each document's old chunks before writing the new ones, so for the whole reindex window that space returned nothing to search. The two generations now live side by side, a durable per-space serving pointer keeps every query answered by the old generation until the new one is fully built, and the switch is an atomic per-space flip — never a global freeze. Also in this release: the permanent test-skip allowlist is back to zero, the MyPy strict-exemption surface shrank 91 → 90, and the frontend cyclomatic-complexity baseline shrank 56 → 53. Backend tests **15,023 → 15,031**.

### Added

- **Generational RAG continuity** (AC-001) — a same-dimension embedding-model change keeps document search available throughout the reindex. `RAGChunk` carries no uniqueness constraint, so the old and new generations coexist; a durable `rag_spaces.serving_embedding_model` column (migration `c1d2e3f4a5b6`, `NULL` = steady state) records which generation each space serves. The reindex pins every space to the old model in the same atomic commit that persists its intent, `process_document` is driven by that pointer so the drain and the reaper never disturb the served generation, and each space flips to the new model atomically once its rebuild completes. A crash mid-reindex is resumed by `flip_pinned_spaces_if_ready` in the RAG job reaper. New metric `rag_reindex_space_flips_total` (`outcome=flipped|deferred|failed`).
- **`langgraph_state` metrics for the router and planner nodes** (AC-007) — `router_node_v3` and `planner_node_v3` now emit the state-update instrumentation the other graph nodes already carried, closing a blind spot in the pipeline's observability.

### Changed

- RAG retrieval groups spaces by the generation actually being served and embeds each query with that generation's model; the global "reindex in progress → skip retrieval" block is removed.
- During a generation swap, `process_document` deletes chunks by `(document, model)` rather than by document alone, so it never removes chunks of the generation still being served.
- A change of embedding **dimension** — which requires a new pgvector column — remains an explicit, documented maintenance window rather than a silent empty result (runbook: [GUIDE_RAG_SPACES](docs/guides/GUIDE_RAG_SPACES.md)).

### Fixed

- RAG semantic search is now wrapped per generation: an embedding or query failure logs `rag_semantic_search_failed`, counts `rag_retrieval_skipped_total{reason="semantic_search_error"}` and degrades to lexical results instead of failing the whole retrieval.
- `reset_rag_embeddings` clears the per-model embedding-client cache alongside the singleton and the query cache, so a reindex can no longer leave a stale client bound to a superseded model.

### Tests

- **8 real-PostgreSQL integration tests** for the generational path: the atomic flip, the crash-resume, and a served-generation query answered by the old model while the new one builds.
- Permanent test-skip allowlist **12 → 0** — the three "dead" connector skips were masking the uncovered `_handle_oauth_connector_callback` delegate branch (0 % covered); four behavioural tests replaced them before deletion.
- MyPy strict-exemption surface **91 → 90** (stale `unused-ignore` and `type: ignore[assignment]` removed) and the frontend cyclomatic-complexity baseline **56 → 53** (`hitl-utils.ts` decomposed into data-driven template tables, behaviour preserved, 20 tests).

## [1.25.20] - 2026-07-25

Security remediation of the 2026-07-13 audit ([ADR-149](docs/architecture/ADR-149-Security-Remediation-Wave-1.md)). Every finding was re-verified against the code before being treated — several were false positives, and the verification exhumed defects the audit had missed. Two controls turned out to be declared but never applied: a skill script inherited the API's Docker group, and the "global rate limit" was an object nothing ever consulted. Backend tests **14,847 → 15,023**.

### Added

- **Skill scripts run in a throwaway container** (SEC-001) — no Docker socket, `--network none`, read-only rootfs with a sized tmpfs, uid 65534, all capabilities dropped, memory/pids/CPU/file-size bounded. The privilege drop it replaces only isolated when the API ran as root; production runs as `appuser`, a member of the `docker` group that a child process inherits — socket included. The script SOURCE is passed inline (`python -c`) rather than mounted: the API is itself a container, so a bind would resolve against the host, and stdin stays free for the JSON payload every skill relies on. An unreachable daemon fails the execution; it never downgrades. Settings: `SKILLS_SCRIPT_SANDBOX`, `_IMAGE`, `_PYTHONPATH`, `_TMPFS_MB`.
- **A global HTTP rate limit that is actually enforced** (SEC-016) — `RateLimitMiddleware`, pure ASGI, backed by the shared `RedisRateLimiter` so the budget is common to the four uvicorn workers. Sized from measurement (a real browser session peaked at 67 req/min; default 300), probes exempt, fail-open when Redis is down with the blind window counted (`http_rate_limit_degraded_total`) and alerted (`GlobalRateLimitDegraded`).
- **Request bodies bounded before they are read** (SEC-031) — `BodySizeLimitMiddleware` refuses on the declared length when it can, and counts streamed bytes when it cannot. Endpoints used to materialise the payload before validating it — on the webhooks, before authenticating it. `Settings` now refuses to boot when the global ceiling sits below a configured upload limit, instead of shipping a remote-only 413 that no endpoint log explains.
- **Every DevOps task is confirmed before it runs** (FN-1) — `claude_server_task_tool` no longer executes: it returns a `DEVOPS_TASK` draft carrying the target server, the full task text and the model-authored `context`, and the SSH session happens in `execute_devops_task_draft` after approval. The draft is the only mechanism both execution modes honour — the pipeline ignores `hitl_required`, and ReAct would otherwise ask twice. Progress streaming is preserved through a `ContextVar` carrying the SSE queue into the executor.
- **Browser requests validated per destination** (SEC-032) — the interceptor checked nothing beyond the scheme and forwarded on exception, so a public page could redirect to loopback, a private range or the metadata service. Each request now resolves its host behind a bounded LRU+TTL verdict cache and fails closed. Behind `BROWSER_SSRF_ENFORCE`, report-only first.
- **Outbound MCP OAuth calls guarded at all five sites** (SEC-008/SEC-030), two of which the audit had not seen — the heuristic endpoint probes and the `WWW-Authenticate` probe. An AST guard now fails the build if any outbound call in that module is left unguarded.
- Profile-image fetching follows redirects **hop by hop** with a per-hop allowlist and a bounded read (SEC-026); the RAG upload proxy authenticates, admits, then reads a strictly bounded body over a single native transport (SEC-006); the static-map proxies require a session and carry their own budget (FN-5); the Telegram webhook refuses when no secret is configured, and the configuration refuses to start on a placeholder (SEC-024).
- Sensitive client storage is purged on logout **and on account change** (SEC-035), via an owner marker that also covers a session expiry followed by a different login.
- GPS parameters (`lat`, `lng`, `origin`, `dest`…) joined the sanitized query parameters, and the uvicorn access loggers are reclaimed so their URLs pass through the PII filter — `uvicorn.access` sets `propagate=False`, so those lines used to bypass it entirely.
- Executable guards for the classes found here: the sandbox argv contract and its fail-closed behaviour, tool-family import order in a fresh interpreter, body-ceiling/upload-ceiling consistency, and MCP outbound-call exhaustiveness.

### Changed

- The SlowAPI `Limiter` and its 429 handler are gone from `main.py`, together with the helpers only their own tests kept alive (`build_default_limit`, `resolve_endpoint_limit`, `get_rate_limit_message`) and the constants that became unreachable with them.
- `draft_executor` split into engine / registry population / leaf registry (`draft_executor_types`), so adding a draft type no longer grows the engine past its size cap.
- The RAG upload proxy reads its ceiling from `RAG_SPACES_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB` — the same `.env` both containers load — instead of a hardcoded copy that would silently reject valid uploads once an operator raised the backend limit.
- `email` is no longer part of `UserUpdate` (SEC-005): the generic profile endpoint has no re-authentication, no proof of owning the new mailbox and no session revocation, so a stolen session could become a permanent takeover through the recovery flow.
- Dev Compose binds its published ports to loopback by default (SEC-015), with `DEV_BIND_HOST_APP` for the app ports when the dev app is reached from the LAN; the deploy script pins host-key checking and tightens the permissions of the credential directory it uploads (SEC-013/SEC-014).

### Fixed

- **A timed-out sandbox container outlived its own timeout.** Killing the `docker run` client does not stop the container, and a script that sleeps burns no CPU — so neither the CPU rlimit nor `--rm` reclaimed it. Each run now carries a unique name and the timeout path force-removes it, from the worker thread so the cleanup survives cancellation of the awaiting coroutine.
- **An import cycle silently removed the whole DevOps tool family at boot.** `drafts.service` imports `agents.tools.output`, which runs the tools package init, which conditionally imports the DevOps module — importing the draft service at module level closed the loop. The unit suite never saw it: importing the module directly takes the safe order.
- **The DevOps confirmation card hid the one field an injection would use.** `context` is model-authored and lands in the remote CLI's `--append-system-prompt`; it is now displayed in full alongside the task.
- **Admin rights were only checked when the draft was built.** An arbitrary delay separates that from the confirmation and a HITL decision can be replayed, so a revoked superuser still got their pending task executed. The check runs again at execution.
- The OAuth `state` is fingerprinted instead of logged verbatim (FN-3), and a daemon refusal (exit 125) is reported as a sandbox failure rather than handing the LLM our image names and daemon state.
- The DevOps guide contradicted itself on `max_turns` — advertised as a working cap in its configuration table, documented as never forwarded three sections below.

### Tests

- **176 new backend tests** covering the sandbox command contract and its fail-closed paths, the DevOps confirmation in both directions, the body-ceiling invariant at its exact boundary, and the import-order regression.
- Non-regression of the skills feature proven by differential rather than by assertion: the ten shipped scripts, executed in both modes with identical parameters, produce **byte-for-byte identical output on nine of ten** (the tenth uses `secrets`).
- The new guards were falsified before being trusted — reintroducing the import cycle reds two of three cases, and removing the outbound guards reds the AST check.

## [1.25.19] - 2026-07-24

Twenty-two silent defects, found by testing the safety mechanisms instead of trusting them. None of them raised, logged or failed a suite: an assistant that ran a bulk action without asking, proactive tool calls that could switch your lights, deleted mail resurfacing in an ordinary search, a rescheduled meeting duplicated instead of moved, and cached tokens billed twice. Backend tests **13,282 → 14,847**.

### Added

- **Twelve executable guards**, each carrying its own oracle rather than a frozen snapshot: connector-parity contract (the `Protocol` file is never imported at runtime, so nothing enforced it), LangGraph state-key declaration, `QueryIntelligence` serialization round-trip, locale-normalization AST guard, display-component XSS/robustness contract parameterized over the card registry, tool-mutation classification vs the declared catalogue category, no initiative-eligible tool is a mutation, the FOR_EACH gate agrees with the mutation oracle, and a cross-stack password-policy parity guard (the browser re-implements the rule; the constants are now pinned against it).
- `display/urls.py` — `safe_url` (scheme allowlist) and `safe_css_color` (hex/keyword allowlist), extracted so every card shares one sanitizer instead of inlining its own.
- `infrastructure/llm/strict_schema.py` — the OpenAI strict-mode schema analysis, extracted from `structured_output.py`.

### Changed

- Coverage gate **45 % → 59 %** (measured 62.79 % on the gated fast-unit subset); frontend thresholds 60/54/54/60 → 62/56/56/62. The margin is deliberate — the measurement is local (Windows) and CI runs on Linux, where a handful of branches differ.
- File-size ratchet re-locked on real gains: `formatters.py` cap 815 → 753, and `structured_output.py` leaves the frozen list entirely (531 SLOC, under the global 600 ceiling).
- `scope_detector` no longer keeps a private copy of the mutation verbs — it delegates to the single oracle, which also removes the drift that caused the FOR_EACH defect below.
- Seven tool manifests now DECLARE their category instead of letting it be inferred from the tool name (`apply_labels`, `complete_task`, `control_hue_light`/`_room`, `activate_hue_scene`, `run_skill_script`, `import_user_skill`).
- Docker build context: `.next-e2e` (2.5 GB), `.mypy_cache`, `htmlcov` and coverage artefacts are excluded — the Web context drops from ~2.9 GB to a few dozen MB.

### Fixed

- **A bulk action could run without ever asking.** Both production call sites pass `is_mutation=False` and let the gate auto-detect from the tool name, but `scope_detector` kept its own verb list, which had drifted from the canonical one: `reply` and `forward` were missing. A mutation needs confirmation from the first iteration, a read-only operation only from the tenth — so "reply to each of these 9 emails" sent **nine replies with no confirmation at all**. Same for forwards, label changes and reminder cancellations.
- **The assistant could act on its own.** The initiative phase (ADR-062) executes tools after a turn to enrich the answer, gated on a category that, absent an explicit declaration, is INFERRED FROM THE TOOL NAME and defaults unknown shapes to read-only. Seven mutating tools were therefore declared safe for proactive execution — including `control_hue_light` (a physical device) and `run_skill_script` (arbitrary code). The "defense in depth" check downstream re-used the very same list, so it verified nothing.
- **Deleted mail resurfaced in ordinary searches.** The trash-exclusion keywords contained the bare words `trash` and `deleted`, matched as substrings: searching "deleted invoices" silently dropped `-in:trash` and mixed trashed messages into the results as if they were live. The operator forms (`in:trash`, `label:TRASH` — what the tool teaches the model to emit) remain honoured, and a whole-query "trash" still maps to the operator.
- **"Reschedule my meeting" created a duplicate instead of moving it.** `reschedule` contains `schedule`, and create is tested before update, so the declared `reschedule` pattern was unreachable: the turn loaded the create tools and never `update_event_tool`. Verified exhaustively — that pair is the only such overlap across the four intent sets.
- **Cached tokens were billed twice.** Providers report an input total that already contains the cache reads; the modern extraction path subtracts them, the legacy path did not, so those tokens were charged at the full input rate on top of the discounted cached rate.
- **A valid plan was rejected as a "ghost dependency".** The check compares the second path segment against the producing step's result_key, but that segment is just as often a plain output FIELD — and `total` is listed in `get_contacts_tool`'s own reference examples. A legitimate reference was therefore refused, forcing a wasted replan.
- **A whole parameter type escaped validation.** `number` was missing from the type table; a type absent from that table is not "unknown, be careful" — it is skipped, and the constraint checks that follow are themselves type-guarded. `get_places_tool.min_rating` had no validation at all, and a string rating only failed inside the tool as `'<=' not supported between float and str`.
- **A tool result keyed `items` broke FOR_EACH in silence.** The polymorphic extractor tested `hasattr` before dict access, so `extract_value({"items": [...]}, "items")` returned the bound `dict.items` METHOD instead of the list — the iteration then ran over nothing, without an error.
- **`javascript:` reached an `href`, and a transit colour escaped its `style` attribute.** Card rendering had no URL-scheme allowlist and interpolated a provider-supplied colour raw: `#fff" onmouseover="…` closed the attribute and injected a handler (proven by parsing the output, not by inspection).
- **Apple/Microsoft connector asymmetries** — a 5xx response was handed to the vCard parser instead of raising (silent data loss on update), a failed delete returned success, `cached_at` was fabricated on every cache hit, and an Outlook folder label failed to match on case/spacing.
- **A locale variant could miss its own table** — seven ad-hoc normalizations (`locale.split("-")[0]`, `language[:2]`) bypassed the single chokepoint, so `zh` never resolved to the backend-canonical `zh-CN`.
- Descending sorts placed rows *missing* the sort key FIRST instead of last, and `DISTINCT` went through a `set`, making result order non-deterministic between runs.
- Nesting-depth analysis for OpenAI strict mode did not follow `$ref`, and Pydantic v2 never inlines nested models — the measured depth was therefore always the shallow one.
- A pytest fixture closed the global psycopg pools on whichever loop the test ran on, including pools opened by an earlier test on another loop, producing a teardown error whenever the unit and agents scopes ran in a single invocation (CI runs them separately, so it only bit locally). It now closes only what the current test opened — which is what its own docstring already promised.

### Tests

- **1,565 new backend tests** across 26 batches, every one written against a behaviour that can fail silently. Each source fix followed the same discipline: a red test proving the defect on real data first, the correction second — never the reverse.
- Targeted coverage on the pieces that decide correctness: plan validation (schema gate, parameter types, conditions, dependency graph, `$steps` references), reference resolution, the entity registry reducer, the HITL resume builder, the draft post-approval sync, connector clients, display cards, Gmail query normalization, outbound-recipient validation, the password policy (which had none) and the LLM cost path.
- Deliberately NOT tested, with the reason recorded: the plan-approval modification path (`approval_gate_node` is an explicit pass-through) and the adaptive replanner (`advisory only, not wired` — no decision changes control flow). Testing them would inflate the number and protect nothing.

## [1.25.18] - 2026-07-24

Factual accuracy of answers (ADR-147/148): grounding on recent entities, weather told in the right time / place / language, correlated results that stop overwriting each other, and health signals that stop vanishing from the heartbeat.

### Added

- **Response grounding on recent entities** ([ADR-147](docs/architecture/ADR-147-Recent-Entities-Grounding.md)) — on a turn producing no `registry_updates`, `{data_for_filtering}` is empty and `<History>` deliberately drops `ToolMessage`, so the response LLM had **no authoritative structured data at all** and could only paraphrase earlier prose. Recent entities are now re-grounded from `state["registry"]` (zero I/O), selected by recency over the `agent_results` keys, capped by `TOOL_CONTEXT_MAX_ITEMS` with a logged truncation, and rendered in a dedicated `<RecentEntities>` prompt section placed AFTER the dynamic marker so the cacheable prefix stays intact. Explicitly non-authoritative (current-turn data wins) and skipped on REFERENCE turns, whose empty registry is an anti-leak fail-safe rather than a grounding hole. Tunable via `RESPONSE_RECENT_ENTITIES_MAX_TURN_AGE` (0 disables).
- **`<DataAuthority>` prompt rule** — forbids inventing an entity attribute, cites `<RecentEntities>` among the authorized sources, and mandates admitting a value that was requested but never received instead of filling it in.
- **Per-day health rollup** ([ADR-148](docs/architecture/ADR-148-Health-Daily-Rollup.md)) — `HealthSampleRepository.fetch_daily_stats` returns one row per UTC day carrying raw integer primitives `(total, count, minimum)`; every `BaselineKind` aggregation derives from them, and because the primitives are exact integers `total / count` is the same IEEE-754 operation as the in-Python `sum / len`, making the equivalence provable rather than merely observed.
- **`heartbeat_source_dropped_total{source,reason}`** — a heartbeat source that fails open leaves no trace in the notification; every drop is now counted and its duration logged (success and failure alike).
- Localized weather tool summaries across the 6 languages (`_WEATHER_SUMMARY_*` in `i18n_v3`), plus an explicit "no detailed forecast for this date" message distinct from the beyond-the-window wording.

### Changed

- Weather three-hour forecasts are mapped to the **user's timezone** before day-bucketing; the rendered `datetime_text` is local and always matches the epoch it ships with.
- The weather tool no longer keeps the request language on the instance — it rides along in the result payload (`_LANGUAGE_RESULT_KEY`), the singleton-state rule that prevents cross-user leaks under concurrency.
- Baselines, variations and the heartbeat health block read the per-day rollup instead of every raw sample: 6 queries / 30,662 rows per tick → 4 queries / ~500 rows. Measured on production-shaped volume: **353 ms → 7.0 ms (×50)**, and the event-loop stall the raw decode caused drops from 124 ms to 1.1 ms.
- `baseline.py` / `signals.py` expose every computation twice over ONE implementation (`*_from_stats` + raw-sample wrappers), so the 19 existing pure-function tests pass unchanged — the non-regression proof is structural, not incidental.
- Extractions to keep frozen files shrinking: `weather_formatting.py` (from `weather_tools`), `plan_predicates.py` (from `semantic_validator`), `health_metrics/heartbeat_signals.py` (from `service.py`, 582→495 SLOC) and `heartbeat/health_context.py` (from `context_aggregator.py`, whose ratchet cap **drops 783 → 753**). `detect_recent_variations` complexity 15 → 10.

### Fixed

- **A tool parameter resolving to nothing became the literal string `"null"`** — the `$item.field` placeholder sits inside the JSON quotes, so emitting `null` produced `"null"`, which every `if not value` guard accepts: production geocoded a town actually named null and answered with the weather of Cappaghnanool, Ireland. A sentinel now marks the missing field and is stripped after parsing, so the parameter reads as absent and the tool applies its own default (auto-geolocation here).
- **A correlated result could erase another one** — tools derive their registry id from content alone (weather → place + day), so two FOR_EACH parents sharing them produced the same id and the accumulator's `dict.update()` silently dropped the first. Measured in production: two appointments both emitting `weather_fee011`, registry stuck at 4 entries instead of 5, one card rendered without the data fetched for it. Ids are now derived per parent (SHA-256 over `item@parent`), deterministic across replays and resumed checkpoints.
- **A date beyond the forecast window returned a silent approximation** instead of an explicit answer, and a within-window date with no provider slot now gets its own message rather than the self-contradicting "only 5 days" wording.
- **Heartbeat health signals were dropped on 46.5 % of ticks** (40 timeouts / 86 decisions over 7 days, silently). PostgreSQL answered in 6.7 ms and the ORM added 58.8 ms — the cost was the per-row client-side decode (~29 µs/row), a synchronous burst that froze the worker's event loop for 483 ms in one stretch. The 2-second budget was being blown by nominal cost, not by a slow database; it is deliberately NOT raised, and its docstring no longer claims to protect against one.
- A single-step plan touching none of the primary domain now triggers semantic validation instead of being waved through; genuine consolidations and multi-step plans are unaffected, and unknown domains or unregistered tools fail open.
- Frontend test `AccountExportSettings` asserted a same-origin download link while merely *assuming* `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` was absent — green in CI (which sets it to `""` at the runner level), red in any developer shell. It now stubs the contract value explicitly.

### Tests

- Golden characterization net for the health baseline/variations pipeline (Feathers method, as ADR-122): 15 datasets × every `window_days` the tools can request (1..14) = 210 pinned service payloads, generated by running the pre-conversion implementation and passed **unchanged** after it. Sensitivity proven by mutation: `DAILY_AVG`→`min` fails 56 entries, the window boundary `<`→`<=` fails 136, and rounding the daily average fails 14 — that last one only caught once repeating-decimal datasets were added, the net having been numerically blind without them.
- Read-path guard on the heartbeat builder: the payload golden cannot see a regression that recomputes the same window twice (output identical, cost doubled), so the number and shape of repository calls is asserted separately — verified by reintroducing the duplicate read.
- Integration tests against a real PostgreSQL: rollup vs in-Python grouping field-for-field, UTC day bucketing across midnight, **session-timezone independence under UTC+14** (removing the explicit `timezone('UTC', …)` fails exactly this test — CI in UTC would never have noticed), window bounds, ordering, and user/kind isolation.
- New suites for weather hourly mapping and localized summaries, correlated-item identity, plan integrity guards, and the response grounding doctrine.

## [1.25.17] - 2026-07-23

Security & account program (D1/D2/D3/D5 — ADR-143/144/145/146): strong authentication, device sessions, GDPR export, offline PWA.

### Added

- **Passkeys (WebAuthn)** — discoverable credentials with conditional UI on the login form (`autocomplete="username webauthn"`) plus an explicit button; enrollment/rename/revocation in Settings > Security; py_webauthn ceremonies with single-use Redis challenges (GETDEL), sign-count clone detection, per-account cap, generic 401 on the whole anonymous path (no credential enumeration). ADR-143.
- **TOTP second factor** — authenticator-app enrollment (backend-rendered QR data-URI, secret revealed once), explicit matched-timestep anti-replay, 10 single-use backup codes (SHA-256 hashes at rest, revealed once, regenerable); two-step login via a single-use 5-min pending token (`/auth/mfa/verify`). ADR-143.
- **Step-up re-authentication** — sensitive actions (MFA management, revoke-others, export, password disabling) require a fresh re-auth within a 5-min window; typed `403 {"error": "step_up_required"}` contract (never a plain 401); verification by password, TOTP/backup code, allow-listed passkey ceremony, or a fresh Google re-sign-in for OAuth-only accounts; a fresh full login opens the window (sudo-mode semantics). Password sign-in can be disabled with ≥ 2 active passkeys (A8; email reset stays the recovery path). ADR-143.
- **"My devices" session management** — session payload v4 with deliberately bounded metadata (browser/OS families, /24-truncated IP, ≥ 15-min-grain last-seen), opaque sha256 display ids, per-device revocation, step-up-guarded revoke-others; a revoked session's SSE streams close within one keepalive tick (fail-open watcher). New-login push notification with FCM-token device attestation (a registered active token suppresses the alert; passkey logins never notify; every failure mode falls toward notifying) + per-user toggle. ADR-144.
- **Full-account GDPR export** — durable `account_export_jobs` consumed by a leader-elected `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` executor (crash-safe stale detection, 24 h retention sweep); metadata-driven builder over the total `user_data_map` classification (EXCLUDED secret tables unexportable BY CONSTRUCTION, column-verified redaction/decryption specs, JSON + readable Markdown, attachments/RAG sources ZIP_STORED, 2 GiB cap, atomic rename); step-up-guarded request, ownership-scoped download, "export ready" push ×6 languages. ADR-145.
- **Offline PWA** — unified service worker (historical `firebase-messaging-sw.js` URL kept for in-place registration updates): push + precached branded offline page (6 inline locales) + stale-while-revalidate for static assets; `/api/`, non-GET, cross-origin and SSE are never cached; `CACHE_VERSION` CI-locked to `package.json`; unconditional registration at app boot (previously only users who enabled push had a SW). ADR-146.
- **Total user-data classification** — `user_data_map.py` (50 tables + 76 users columns, purge/export policies) with a 10-test CI guard; deletion purge extended to `open_loops` and `phone_calls` (soft-deleted users never fire CASCADE).
- **`task dev:trust-cert`** — extracts the dev TLS certificate and trusts it (Windows `certutil`): Chromium refuses every WebAuthn ceremony on an untrusted certificate; documented with its three traps in GETTING_STARTED.
- CI guard `test_env_example_inline_comment_guard.py` — inline comments on EMPTY-valued env vars poison the runtime (docker compose AND Task dotenv pass the comment as the value); caught 33 pre-existing offenders on arrival, all fixed (+10 in local `.env`, including a `DOCKER_HOST` that broke every task-launched docker command).

### Changed

- Settings > Security redesigned as three standard collapsible `SettingsSection` cards (Strong authentication / My devices / Export my data) matching every other settings section.
- `create_session` stamps `step_up_at` at creation — right after signing in, no re-auth dialog for 5 minutes; this also un-deadlocks OAuth-only accounts enrolling their first factor.
- Metadata-driven purge: `build_purge_statements` now works on Table objects (no ORM imports) — the import-cycle ratchet SHRANK 31→25.
- Sessions no longer auto-refresh their TTL (fixed 7/30-day lifetime); dead `refresh_session` removed and the five false "auto-refresh" claims corrected.
- Export download link targets the API origin via the new `apiEndpointUrl()` helper (top-level navigation streaming to disk — archives are never fetched into a blob).

### Fixed

- Step-up dialog dead end for OAuth-only accounts (only "Cancel" shown): the account's identity provider is now advertised and usable as a step-up method, and an explanatory empty state replaced the bare Cancel.
- A mistyped password/code in the step-up dialog ejected the user to /login: `/auth/step-up/*` 401s are exempt from the api-client's global redirect (inline error + retry), pinned by `api-client.step-up-401.test.ts`.
- Export "Download archive" produced a dead `download.txt`: the href was relative to the frontend origin, which has no `/api/v1` routes.
- Concurrent export requests: the race loser hit the partial unique index as a raw 500 — now the same 400 as the pre-check.
- `docker compose` passes `KEY=   # comment` as the VALUE when the value is empty: the dev WebAuthn rpId became a comment string; fail-fast validator + comments moved above empty vars everywhere.
- Login-notification preference had no UI and the frontend never sent the FCM attestation token: both wired (Settings > My devices toggle; silent token resolution at login when push permission is already granted).

### Tests

- Backend 12,906 collected (fast suite 11,082 passed / 0 failed), MyPy strict clean (971 files); frontend 2,533 passed (259 files), tsc clean, a11y/react-hooks/CC ratchets hold (CC lowered 57→56); hermetic e2e 44/44 including a CDP virtual-authenticator passkey ceremony; 4 replay-checked migrations (head `b9d5f7a32c84`); runtime-proven on the dev stack (real TOTP enrollment, real passkey ceremony after trusting the dev cert, real export download).

## [1.25.16] - 2026-07-23

> **Ten UX refinements, six QA fixes, one adversarial review — the conversation surface grows up.** This release ships a complete UX program (10 lots, each landed with tests, gates and live runtime proof) plus the same-day QA feedback and a full staged-code review whose 12 findings were all fixed before this commit. The chat learns the manners of a mature messenger: a persistent per-user draft, ↑/↓ recall over the last ten sends, an action row under every answer (copy, feedback, and the execution trace docked at its right edge), tappable follow-up chips generated by the Initiative node, `/` slash commands with everyday shortcuts, and a **reading invariant** — a streaming answer never yanks a reader who scrolled up (an explicit own-send signal replaced two data-diff heuristics that both false-fired against the real engine; a gate-promise SSE e2e caught all three bugs unit tests could not). The dashboard becomes yours: the 9 briefing cards can be hidden and reordered (a hidden card is never fetched — the economy is server-side), a starter checklist exposes the instance's dormant capabilities, and the open-loops ledger gets a consult/close surface. LIA becomes installable: 6 localized PWA manifests, real icons, OS share-target into a chat draft, and a discreet install hint. Skills get a gallery (detail sheet, preview endpoint, declared output channels — the loader finally reads the `outputs:` field the generator had validated all along) and **install-from-URL** through the reused SSRF validator (https-only, DNS-resolved block ranges, no redirects, streamed cap, total transfer deadline, per-user rate limit) feeding the untouched hardened import pipeline. And the journal's compiled portrait now speaks the user's language — the English voice examples buried in the consolidation prompt were overriding the language instruction 150 lines above; the fix binds `{user_language}` at every generation point, proven by regenerating a real French portrait in place.

### Added

- **Chat input maturity (A7)** — per-user persistent draft (`lia.chatDraft.{userId}`, debounced, clamped at the backend cap, purged on logout, `?draft=` deep links persisted at consumption) and an ↑/↓ walk over the last 10 sent messages (consecutive-duplicate collapse; editing the recalled text returns the arrows to the caret; IME-safe).
- **Bubble action row (PERSO)** — copy + response feedback in flow at the bubble's bottom (the old overlay covered text on mobile), with the execution trace (« N steps · X s ») docked at the row's right edge and its panel expanding full-width (QA feedback).
- **Reading invariant + floating return (A3)** — live-geometry follow decision (`lib/chat-scroll.ts`, growth-compensated bottom detection), floating "back to bottom" button with an off-screen-responses badge (counted once per response, polite live region), history-view delegation to return-to-present; hermetic gate-promise SSE e2e (`chat-scroll-follow.spec.ts`).
- **Follow-up chips (A2)** — the Initiative node emits 0-3 sanitized suggestions (server-side clamp/dedupe, pop-once per-run handoff — the service state is a pre-run snapshot), carried in BOTH the SSE done chunk and the archived metadata; a chip click prefills, never sends.
- **Slash commands (A4)** — hand-built WAI-ARIA combobox on the native textarea (no cmdk), diacritic-insensitive filtering on localized label aliases, conversational commands prefill / local commands navigate; catalogue: resume, briefing, agenda, search + everyday shortcuts (emails, weather, weekend weather, tasks, reminders, news) + dialogue-flagged skills.
- **Briefing grid preferences (B4)** — hide/reorder the 9 dashboard cards (`users.briefing_preferences` JSONB, strict PUT schema + tolerant reader completing the canonical order); a hidden card short-circuits BEFORE any fetch or cache IO and refuses direct refresh (`section_hidden`); keyboard-first settings UI (↑/↓ buttons, polite position announcement AFTER the successful persist, drag-and-drop as pointer enhancement). `RefreshSectionLiteral` repaired from a silent 6/9 drift and completeness-pinned.
- **Starter checklist (A10)** — dismissible "getting started" card with live-detected items gated on instance flags (`/config` grows `channels/heartbeat/skills/open_loops_enabled`); only dismissal/celebration timestamps are persisted (`users.onboarding_checklist`, stamp-once on true transitions), pre-completed profiles are stamped silently.
- **Open-loops surface (B5)** — settings section listing the commitments ledger grouped by direction with one-tap Done / Relaunch-in-chat (draft prefill) / No-longer-relevant (`closed_reason=dismissed`, API-validated `Literal`); closure counters at the repository chokepoint (`open_loop_closures_total{reason}`); 404 = surface absent, transient failures get a retry affordance.
- **PWA installability + share (A6)** — 6 localized manifests (start_url, shortcuts ×3, separate any/maskable icon entries, structural parity pinned by test), real PNG icons + apple-touch-icon (iOS ignores SVG), per-locale `<link rel=manifest>` via `generateMetadata` (SEO fields byte-preserved and unit-guarded), OS share-target `GET /{lng}/share` composing a clamped chat draft (never auto-sent), and an install hint (≥3 visits, never in standalone, dismissible forever).
- **Skills gallery + install-from-URL (B12)** — card grid opening a detail sheet (localized description, declared channels with "text" fallback, `assets/preview.png` served by a dedicated endpoint with name-pattern traversal guard + size cap + admin-disabled 404, provenance warning on every non-admin skill); `POST /skills/import-from-url` (https-only, reused `web_fetch` SSRF validator, redirects refused, streamed size cap, TOTAL transfer deadline, per-user Redis rate limit, magic-byte/frontmatter sniffing, stable `url_*` error contract) feeding `SkillImportService.import_upload` verbatim; `skill_url_imports_total{outcome}`. The loader now surfaces the declarative `outputs:` frontmatter field (generator-parity pinned — recorded deviation from the planned `channels:` name: the vocabulary already existed).
- **Telephony in the connectors administration** — `elevenlabs_telephony` added to the frontend connector tables and the admin section (own category, i18n ×6); the backend enum had it since telephony P1.

### Fixed

- **Journal portrait/entries in English for non-English users** — the consolidation prompt's English voice examples ("I notice…") overrode the language instruction 150 lines above; `{user_language}` is now bound at every generation point (voice line, brief spec, JSON schema) and the introspection prompt hardened; proven by regenerating a real portrait in French in place.
- **Page-level scrollbar regression** — the Lot 3 `sr-only` live region (position:absolute, no positioned ancestor) escaped the thread scroller's clipping and stretched the BODY; fixed with a zero-height relative containing block.
- **Floating button inert after a quiet start** — the scroll listener now arms at pin-window expiry and on the first user gesture, not only when content overflowed during the window (review finding).
- **Checklist PATCH replay** — timestamps stamp on true transitions only; a retried/second-tab PATCH no longer rewrites history (and no longer commits).
- **Slash-menu highlight** — re-filtering returns the highlight to the first option instead of a clamped leftover position.
- **Day-of-release Next.js advisories** — four high-severity advisories published against Next 16 (App Router middleware/proxy bypass, Server Actions DoS + SSRF, rewrites SSRF — GHSA-6gpp-xcg3-4w24, GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj, GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x et al.) red the blocking dependency audit; bumped to 16.2.11 (patch release), lockfile refreshed, high-level audit clean.
- **Review hardening** — total transfer deadline on URL imports (httpx timeouts are per-phase; a dripping server was unbounded in time), per-user rate limit on outbound fetches (failed imports consume no skill quota), preview 404 for admin-disabled system skills, chat-search focus scoped to its own `data-chat-search` marker, English-only API field descriptions, and the repo's infra-info guard caught a real private IP in a new SSRF test (replaced by a neutral RFC 1918 address).

### Changed

- `ExecutionTraceDisclosure` renders inside the action row (fragment, `ml-auto` toggle, full-width wrap panel) instead of a separate line under the bubble.
- `SkillsSettings` decomposed into `SkillGallery` / `SkillDetailModal` / `ImportFromUrlDialog` + top-level handler factories (frontend CC baseline locked LOWER: 51 files ≥15, was 52); `auth/router.py` growth refused by the SLOC ratchet — the checklist endpoint lives in its own `auth/checklist_router.py`.
- E2e scroll spec waits on observable geometry (`expect.poll`) instead of arbitrary sleeps (the two pin-window sleeps are structural and documented).

### Tests

- **10,972 backend** (fast suite; +66: outputs field + generator parity, URL-import SSRF matrix + total-deadline + endpoint passthrough + rate limit, preview guard, checklist stamp-once, briefing preferences/hidden sections, followup metadata, open-loops router) + **2,465 frontend** (249 files; +141 across chat-scroll decisions, input draft/history walk, slash commands/menu, follow-up chips, briefing grid, checklist, open loops, install hint, PWA manifests structural parity, gallery flow) — tsc clean non-incremental, a11y/react-hooks/CC ratchets hold (CC locked lower). Playwright: scroll-follow 2/2 (caught 3 real bugs during development) + full smoke 29/29 against the dev container. Two Alembic migrations (`briefing_preferences`, `onboarding_checklist`) replayed down+up in-container. Runtime proof for every lot on the dev stack, including real SSRF refusals (private IP 400, HTML 422, GitHub SKILL.md 409 through the S2 pipeline, oversized zip 413) with all four outcomes visible in `/metrics`.

## [1.25.15] - 2026-07-22

> **The showcase learns to fit in your hand.** The landing page claimed "responsive" while silently amputating itself on phones: the hero clipped its own CTAs, the whole layout **oscillated between 381px and 448px during the animation cycle** (the mockup's typing text inflated its grid track on every act — invisible on any static screenshot), and chapter 01 cut every benefit line mid-word at 412px for a 375px viewport. One root cause explains all of it — flex/grid children whose intrinsic min-content width widens the track (`truncate` without `min-w-0`, chip rows without wrap) while `html { overflow-x: hidden }` turns the overflow into silent clipping instead of a scrollbar. The fix is a doctrine, not a patch: `min-w-0` on every two-column track, wrap on every variable-count row — and a Playwright guard that replays the **full 79-second animation cycle in virtual time**, asserting the invariant at every beat (it promptly caught a fourth, unrelated bug: the carousel dots overflow the 320px WCAG reflow floor). The public FAQ sheds its unstyled-`<details>` look for the landing's own visual language — search, icon section rail, 51 questions instead of 13 — and the infamous 10,000-character "What can I ask LIA?" wall (8,883px tall on a phone) becomes twelve per-domain sub-accordions **without touching one translated word**: the grouping is a presentation-only parser whose test proves word-for-word equality across all 6 real locales (zh, whose q4 is a different answer, falls back untouched). The four-act hero animation gets its own shareable URL (`/demo` — no header, no auth redirect, zero new i18n keys) plus a 1080×1350 H.264 export for social feeds, and both redesigned pages join the axe gate: zero critical/serious violations, contrast included, light AND dark.

### Added

- **`/demo`** — the hero conversation animation as a standalone localized public page (6 languages, hreflang + canonical + OG, no header/footer/auth-redirect), built for social sharing and embeds; reuses existing copy only (`landing.meta.title` + `landing.chat_mockup.aria` — zero new translation keys). Registered in `PUBLIC_ROUTE_SEGMENTS` (the completeness guard caught the omission: a 401 would have bounced visitors to /login) and in the sitemap. A social MP4 export procedure ships in `docs/technical/LANDING_PAGE.md` (Playwright recordVideo — viewport MUST equal the video size, the mismatched-size rescale squeezes the frame — then ffmpeg H.264; artifacts under gitignored `exports/`).
- **Public FAQ redesign** (`/faq`) — landing visual language: accent-insensitive search (helpers extracted to `lib/faq-search.ts`, shared with the dashboard FAQ), chip anchor rail, icon section headers (`components/faq/faq-sections.ts` — shared registry), native `<details>` cards, `prose` answer typography (links were invisible before). Public scope grows from 2 sections/13 questions to **6 sections/51 questions** (getting started, connectors, telephony, voice, image generation, privacy — the pre-signup set), JSON-LD included.
- **`lib/faq-answer-groups.ts`** — presentation-only splitter turning `<br><br><strong>`-shaped mega-answers into per-domain collapsible groups (the 10.9k-char q4 renders 747px instead of 8,883px). Translation files byte-identical; `faq-answer-groups.test.ts` proves readable-text equality on all 6 locales and the zh fallback.
- **Landing mobile overflow guard** (`e2e/smoke/landing-mobile-overflow.spec.ts`) — at 375px: static, then across the whole hero animation cycle via the Playwright clock (79s virtual — the oscillation class is only visible with the timeline running), then per scrolled section; plus a 320px WCAG 1.4.10 reflow pass.
- **Public-pages axe gate** (`e2e/a11y/axe-public-pages.spec.ts`) — `/faq` (with a grouped answer open) and `/demo`, light and dark (the theme is localStorage-driven — `defaultTheme="light"` means OS-scheme emulation does nothing; the spec encodes the trap).

### Fixed

- **Hero clipped and unstable on phones** — the badge row (`whitespace-nowrap` version pill in a no-wrap flex) forced the column to 381px/343 available: version truncated, title off-center, subtitle cut mid-word, both CTAs bleeding off-screen; and the mockup's typing input (`truncate` without `min-w-0`) periodically snapped the whole hero to 448px during acts. Fixed with `flex-wrap` + `min-w-0` on both grid tracks and the mockup's inflating rows (input bar, backstage query pill and chips) — column now measures a constant 343px across the full cycle.
