- **Chapter 01 text cut at the right edge** — the vignette's three-chip row (min-content 412px) and its truncated query pill (383px) widened the chapter grid track past the viewport; every benefit line rendered clipped. `min-w-0` on the `ChapterSection` grid items and the vignette chips/pill (chapters 02–05 were already clean; measured).
- **Carousel dots overflow the 320px reflow floor** — 12–15 × 24px dot targets in a no-wrap row (screenshots + slides carousels); found by the new guard's WCAG pass, fixed with `flex-wrap`.
- **Mobile hero typography** — h1 starts at `text-4xl` (was `text-5xl` on 343px), and the subtitle's forced `<br>`/`\n` breaks now apply only from the `mobile` breakpoint up (no more orphan words); desktop rendering pixel-identical.
- **React duplicate-key errors on the public FAQ** — identical bullet strings within a grouped answer collided as keys (caught in the runtime console during proof); index keys are correct for this static, never-reordered list.
- **`llms.txt` audit-score drift** — claimed 8.0/10 while the published audit (and the landing) say 8.3/10; metrics realigned with `LANDING_STATS`.

### Changed

- `FAQContent` (dashboard) now imports the shared search helpers and section-icon registry instead of owning them (−146 lines, behavior pinned by its existing suite).

### Tests

- **12,717 backend** (untouched) + **2,324 frontend** (233 files; +19: answer-groups parser ×13, public FAQ behavior ×6) — tsc clean non-incremental, a11y/react-hooks/CC ratchets hold. New Playwright evidence in the official image: overflow guard 3/3 (including the 79s virtual-time cycle), axe public pages 4/4 light+dark, zero critical/serious. Runtime proof on the dev container: hero column stable at 343px through the full cycle (was 381↔448px), zero in-flow element past the viewport on all 13 sections, grouped q4 at 747px (was 8,883px), desktop pixel-identical.

## [1.25.14] - 2026-07-22

> **The psyche becomes measurable — and the third fix ships with its own referee.** ADR-104 de-saturated the assistant's mood a month ago and promised a production re-measurement that was never instrumented; this release starts by paying that debt. A deterministic replay of the real engine plus a computation over the real 14-personality catalogue exposed two defects the previous pass could not see: the **dominance axis is structurally off-center** (all 14 personalities — including the one literally named _Dépressif_ — rest on the assertive side; five of the fourteen moods are unreachable at rest, and damping, being a homothety, can NEVER recenter them), and the **proactive joy pulse crowns an emotion the LLM never reported** (55% of ordinary-regime turns — the exact mechanism of the pride pulse ADR-104 removed). Both fixes ship as `.env` knobs **defaulting to today's behavior**: merging changes nothing, and a golden characterization test freezes all 14 resting points at 1e-9 to prove it. The missing instrument now exists (`measure_psyche.py`, read-only, runnable via `docker exec` in prod — its first dev-DB run confirmed the lock on live data: 4/14 moods, 100% single-octant, 99.3% dominant-emotion stickiness) and a CI reachability oracle replays a scripted conversation through the real engine so the properties become permanent rules instead of hand-tuned numbers. The kindalive project that triggered the investigation was examined mechanism by mechanism and **rejected on measurement** — its analytical lens (resting points need headroom on both sides) is what found the defect; its architecture added nothing. (ADR-142)

### Added

- **Psyche measurement instrument** (`apps/api/scripts/measure_psyche.py`): the ADR-104 baseline battery per user (distinct moods visited, PAD octant coverage, D<0/A<0 shares, dominant-emotion distribution with joy/pride flags, intensity ≥ 0.60 share, stickiness, co-active mean, post-idle magnitude) + live personality-catalogue resting table at current settings. Read-only, no PII, `--json-out` for before/after diffing; ships inside the api image (`apps/api/scripts/`, not repo-root `scripts/`).
- **`PSYCHE_DOMINANCE_CENTER`** (default `0.0` = inert): post-damping translation of the dominance resting point, threaded through all 6 baseline call sites. The activation candidate `0.20` is _derived_ from the measured catalogue mean (+0.216), not guessed; at that value 7/14 personalities rest D < 0 with the personality ordering exactly preserved and P/A untouched.
- **`PSYCHE_PROACTIVE_JOY_PULSE`** (default `true` = inert): gate on the sustained-quality joy pulse so the LLM-reported appraisal can own the emotion channel; `curiosity`/`enthusiasm` pulses (measured near-inert, legitimately scoped) are kept.
- **Mood-reachability CI guards** (`test_mood_reachability.py`): golden no-op characterization of the 14 catalogue resting PADs (frozen at 1e-9, actionable failure message), catalogue-straddle guard at the recommended center (≥ 5 personalities each side of D=0, ordering preserved), and a deterministic end-to-end oracle (30-turn scripted ordinary regime through the real engine: 3 moods/87% top at today's default, ≥ 5 moods/≤ 70% top at 0.20). The catalogue is loaded from the seeding migration via importlib — single source of truth, no duplicated table.
- **ADR-142** — full decision record with explicit epistemic caveats (synthetic-stream magnitudes vs production-confirmed facts), the measured activation procedure, and a readjustment decision matrix (character fidelity via `pad_dominance_override`, 0.15 fallback).

### Fixed

- **Honesty micro-fixes** (comments/docstrings only, zero behavior): `PsycheStateRepository.update` claimed "optimistic locking via updated_at" over a plain flush — the docstring now documents the actual flush semantics and the known pre/post-response writer race; `PsycheState` trait comments no longer claim independent evolution; `narrative_identity` and `trait_snapshot` Python comments state what the columns actually hold (weekly narrative; dynamic state, not Big Five) — SQL column comments kept verbatim to avoid model/DB drift, reconciliation deferred to the next periodic comment migration.

### Tests

- **12,717 backend** (10,893 fast-unit green incl. all ratchet guards; mypy strict clean on 945 files — plus explicit black/ruff/mypy on the new script, which sits outside the `src`/`tests` gate perimeter) + **2,305 frontend** (untouched, suite green as zero-impact proof). 24 new psyche tests (dominance-center unit ×5, joy-gate ×3, CI guards ×9, measurement aggregators ×12, minus shared fixtures); psyche domain suite 207 green. Runtime proof: script executed in-container against the dev DB; api container healthy after restart with both new settings loaded at their no-op values.

## [1.25.13] - 2026-07-22

> **The assistant learns to connect its domains.** One product analysis of the whole codebase yielded 17 cross-domain proposals; the six delivered lots (ADR-139/140/141) close the highest-value gaps. LIA now keeps a **commitments ledger**: "je dois rappeler le plombier" quietly becomes an open loop — extracted after the answer by a fifth background pass, nudged by the heartbeat with an anti-nag cooldown, closed the day you say "c'est fait" (flag OFF by default). "Fais-moi une revue de presse tous les matins" finally works **from the chat**: a confirmable draft creates the recurring automation, and a deterministic recurrence detector notices "same ask, same hour, three distinct days" and offers the automation before you think of it. The **user's documents become an active domain** — the planner can chain "compare the PDF quote with Paul's email" — and one call builds a **person-360 overview** (contact card + recent mails + shared events + memories, honestly partial per connector). The briefing grows from six to **nine cards**: "For you" (open loops + automations digest with the precise next run time), strictly pending/overdue **Tasks** (date-only local semantics — due today is never "overdue"), and latest-modified Drive **Documents** (summarize in chat, or open in Drive). The heartbeat gains birthdays with a proposed action chain, journals-grade dynamic memories, an anti-repetition window that finally sees reminders/automations/call reports, a traffic-aware **departure alert** ("pars vers 13:30 — 30 min de trajet"), locally-anchored interests ("expo à Lyon ce week-end") and a meeting-prep nudge — and a completed phone call now proposes the calendar entry it agreed on. Four successive "are you fully satisfied?" counter-reviews caught 15 real defects before release — among them a Redis budget key built on process-randomized `hash()`, six leaked httpx transports (three of them pre-existing in the heartbeat, one per source per cycle), and debug caches whose TTL eviction ran only on a read path that a debug-panel-less deployment never executes.

### Added

- **Open-loops commitments ledger** (ADR-139, `OPEN_LOOPS_ENABLED=false`): `open_loops` table + migration, post-response LLM extraction (dedup, per-user cap, conversational closure), 12th heartbeat source with due/stale nudge policy and per-loop cooldown, minimal REST surface (list + close), For-you card block, debug-panel section.
- **Chat-piloted automations** (ADR-140, creation always on; `RECURRENCE_SUGGESTION_ENABLED=false` for the detector): `create_scheduled_action` returns a confirmable SCHEDULED_ACTION draft (HITL card with localized schedule), `list`/`toggle` tools, Redis recurrence ledger (4-hour local buckets, distinct-days threshold, one-shot cooldown) surfacing an automation suggestion through the initiative slot.
- **Active knowledge layer** (ADR-141): routable `document` domain over the user's RAG spaces (`search_user_documents`, deployment-gated) and cross-domain `get_person_overview` (4 parallel sub-fetches on own sessions, `partial_failures` honesty).
- **Briefing 2.0 — nine cards**: « For you » (fuchsia; loops deep-link the chat with direction-aware intents; automations digest shows the **precise next execution time**, reminders formatting doctrine), **Tasks** (teal; multi-provider Google/Microsoft with preferred list; overdue-first; chat intents progress/reschedule), **Documents** (indigo; Drive modifiedTime desc; summarize-in-chat + external Drive link). Portrait-informed synthesis (`user_model_block`).
- **Heartbeat intelligence**: birthdays source with proposed action chain (message/call), dynamic second-pass memories (ADR-135 symmetry), extended anti-redundancy window covering reminders/scheduled-action results/call reports, traffic-aware departure advice (`HEARTBEAT_DEPARTURE_ENABLED=false`; Routes ETA, leave-by, per-(user,event) Redis cache), locally-anchored interest content (`INTERESTS_LOCAL_ANCHOR_ENABLED=false`), meeting-prep nudge (rule 21), post-call appointment suggestion appended to the telephony return.
- **Cross-domain chains guidance**: adjacency matrix completed (event↔task, email→file, document domain) + explicit chain few-shots in the planner and ReAct prompts (place→call, event→route+weather, email→file, task→event).
- **Debug panel**: Open Loop Extraction section; one aggregation chokepoint (`pop_background_extraction_debug`) so a new extraction family costs zero churn at the SSE emission site.
- **Chat header**: message search is left-aligned; the offline/processing pill sits left of it (hermetic Playwright guard pins the arrangement).

### Changed

- `related_domains` false comment fixed and matrix entries corrected (the initiative node's reverse lookup is now documented at the consumer).
- Initiative wrapper (`initiative_recurrence`) mounts the historical core untouched and merges the deterministic recurrence suggestion only when the LLM produced none.
- Geocoding moved to `connectors/geocoding.py` (heartbeat shim kept) — breaks the heartbeat↔interests runtime cycle; birthdays computation moved to `connectors/birthdays.py` (briefing wrapper keeps its section-status contract).
- `_validate_read_only` (initiative) now also drops exact duplicate (tool, parameters) actions — the LLM occasionally emitted the same weather check twice.

### Fixed

- **Transport leaks (6 sites)**: `person_tools` sub-fetches (×3), `connectors/birthdays` full scan, and the pre-existing heartbeat calendar/tasks/emails fetchers (one leaked httpx client per source per cycle) — all now `try/finally: close()`.
- **Departure ETA cache key** was built on Python's process-randomized `hash()` — every worker/restart missed the cache and re-paid the Routes call; now a pinned sha1 recipe.
- **Extraction debug caches** (journals + open loops) evicted stale entries only in `pop()` — a deployment that never opens the debug panel never pops, so the dict grew one entry per turn for the process lifetime; eviction now runs on the write path.
- Naive LLM `due_hint` timestamps are coerced to aware-UTC (timestamptz doctrine); the extraction prompt now demands an offset.
- `bump_nudged` enforces loop ownership in the WHERE clause (close_loop doctrine).
- `NoLocationAvailableError` is a silent expected gate for departure advice (was a warning every cycle); hardcoded `"fr"` fallback replaced by `settings.default_language`.
- Dead code removed (`OpenLoopStatusFilter`, unused `locality` parameter); recurrence-ledger docstrings realigned with the 4-hour bucket reality.

### Tests

- **12,688 backend** (10,867 unit green incl. all ratchet guards; migration replay-check OK; mypy strict clean on 945 files) + **2,305 frontend** (3 ratchets hold; i18n parity ×6). New suites: open loops (models/repository/router/extractor/wiring), recurrence ledger + suggestion wiring, scheduled-action draft golden, birthdays, departure advice, person/documents/automation tools, For-you/Tasks/Documents cards, provider-client lifecycle (briefing + heartbeat + person tools), header layout Playwright guard.

## [1.25.12] - 2026-07-22

> **Six quick wins move the daily surfaces from consultative to actionable.** The ⚙ execution trace used to die with the page: server-side capture now mirrors the live accumulator step for step (same reset, same per-key dedup, i18n keys only — the PII guard is structural, free text has no slot to land in) and the reloaded bubble shows the same "N steps · X s" disclosure the user watched live. The amber "Reconnect" banner used to fire only on the run that broke the connector; on every later run the tool just said "no connector" — resolution-time detection closes that gap, through two paths because the audit found the dominant one **returns** its error instead of raising it. History search stops lying by omission: accent-insensitive on both ends (`unaccent` was already installed — only the query never used it), match counter, in-bubble highlighting through a post-sanitize rehype plugin (the FAQ highlighter is `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` — unusable on LLM output), and a whole-history panel whose results jump into place with a keyset `+1 ms` cursor and an honest "back to present" path. The briefing cards become buttons that open the chat prefilled with a contextual intent; the compiled portrait — one of the product's most singular artifacts, buried three levels deep — gains a settings shortcut, a dashboard hint and an onboarding mention; and ordinary responses finally get the 👍/👎 the proactive notifications always had, wired into the journals' evidence/contradiction counters through an injected port — because the naïve import closed a domain cycle and the F009 guard said no. Two ratchets moved the right way: the streaming hotspot shrank under its frozen cap, and the frontend CC baseline was LOWERED (max 74 → 60).

### Added

- **Persisted execution trace (ADR-133 V2)** — `services/streaming/trace_capture.py` observes the exact chunks the frontend renders live, at the single per-chunk chokepoint of the streaming loop: reset + router seed on `router_decision`, one occurrence per `i18n_key` per turn (the live bubble early-returns on seen keys — a FOR_EACH shows ONE tool step, so does the persisted trace), `reasoning`/`tool_error` excluded, tail-keeping cap via `EXECUTION_TRACE_PERSIST_MAX_STEPS` (default 100 = frontend `MAX_TRACE_STEPS`). Attached branch-free at archive next to the widget persistence (`with_persisted_trace`, `FIELD_EXECUTION_TRACE`, `duration_ms`); hydrated by `lib/execution-trace-hydration.ts`, which re-resolves labels from the stored keys — same `ExecutionTrace` type, same disclosure component, zero render fork. A reloaded trace deliberately has no 💭 block: the reasoning stream is never persisted.
- **Reconnect banner at provider resolution (ADR-134 V2)** — `find_error_connector_type()` consults the same Redis-cached connector list as the resolver and reports a category connector stuck in `status=ERROR` (`REVOKED` deliberately ineligible: a chosen disconnection must not be nagged about). Two emission paths because `handle_tool_exception` is sync: `ConnectorNotEnabledError` is enriched **at raise time** (`build_connector_not_enabled_error` — HITL executes, tasks, contacts) and read by the classifier as a plain attribute; `ConnectorTool.execute`, which _returns_ its category error without raising, emits the notice directly (`emit_connector_notice`, now a public single emitter). Same SSE contract, same metric, same frontend banner.
- **Complete history search (QW-2)** — backend `unaccent(content) ILIKE unaccent(pattern)` with LIKE wildcards escaped ("50%" now matches the literal text); the contract-locking integration test rewritten to pin all three dimensions (case, accents both directions, literal wildcards). Frontend: instant accent-insensitive filter over the loaded window + "N results in loaded messages" counter; in-bubble `<mark class="lia-search-mark">` via `rehype-search-highlight` running after `rehypeKatex` (skips code/KaTeX; plain `indexOf` on the normalized text — user input is never a pattern; original characters stay marked: searching "reunion" highlights "RÉUNION"); "Search entire history" panel (keyset-paginated dated excerpts, React-segment highlighting, no HTML injection anywhere) with jump-to-result (`before = created_at + 1 ms`), an amber history-view banner, "back to present", and a send wrapper that returns to the present before a new turn lands. Mobile (< 880 px): a header 🔍 unfolds the input row. 15 i18n keys × 6 languages.
- **Actionable briefing cards (QW-9)** — mail, agenda, birthday and reminder items become real, labelled `<button>`s (the accessible name IS the intent) that open the chat prefilled through the onboarding `?draft=` deep-link, generalized (`chatDraftHref`): _"Résume-moi le mail « {sujet} » de {expéditeur} et propose une réponse"_, _"Prépare-moi pour « {titre} » de {heure}"_, _"Prépare un message d'anniversaire pour {nom}"_ — reminders open the chat plainly. The consumed `?draft=` is stripped from the URL (`history.replaceState`), which also fixes the onboarding's latent re-prefill on F5.
- **Portrait discoverability (QW-10)** — `?section=` generalized (value → tab + accordion + scroll, via stable `settings-section-<value>` anchors on `SettingsSection`); "What LIA understands about you" shortcut at the head of Identity & Memory (rendered only when a compiled portrait exists — no teaser), backed by a light `useJournalPortrait` hook gateable on the `journals_enabled` flag now exposed in the frontend `AppConfig` type; a discreet dashboard hint under the hero when the portrait was recompiled within 7 days (localStorage keyed by `compiled_at`, so a NEWER compilation re-surfaces it); a portrait mention on the onboarding Memory page.
- **Response feedback on ordinary responses (QW-5, ADR-138)** — `POST /conversations/me/messages/{id}/feedback`: verdict (+ optional 👎 comment) persisted by an atomic owner-scoped `jsonb_set` (the `mark_interest_feedback_submitted` pattern; foreign/non-assistant ids → 404, existence hidden). The `done` chunk carries `archived_message_id` (the archive precedes the done — verified), history rows carry `message_db_id`; the turn's `injected_journal_ids` are archived with the message (IDs only) so a later verdict feeds the evidence/contradiction counters of exactly the entries that shaped the answer — **first verdict only** (counters have no decrement path; changing the verdict updates the stored verdict, never re-feeds). A 👎 comment additionally lands as an L0 `user_correction` entry **without** consolidation (no LLM cost per thumb). Journal side-effects go through an injected port (`JournalFeedbackHooks` + `journals/feedback_hooks.py`, registered at startup): the direct import — even lazy — closed the `conversations↔journals` domain cycle and the F009 guard caught it. `response_feedback_total{verdict}` is the first direct satisfaction metric on ordinary responses. UI: 👍/👎 chips next to Copy (hover-revealed on desktop, visible on mobile, `aria-pressed` on the active verdict), hydrated cross-device, one-line "what went wrong?" unfolded on 👎 — and never an automatic regeneration.

### Fixed

- **Chat header hygiene (QW-12)** — the green "online" pill pulsed permanently while carrying information only in its rare states: the nominal state is now silent (offline and processing keep their pills). The conversation-totals banner no longer costs a full line: totals (TOTAL/IN/OUT/CACHE/GOOGLE, message count, cost) folded into the context pill's tooltip with the `tokens_display_enabled` gating intact. The now-orphaned `chat.input.status.online` key removed from the 6 locales.
- **LIKE wildcards in history search** — an unescaped `ilike(f"%{search}%")` made "50%" match any content containing "50"; `%`, `_` and `\` are literals now.
- **Onboarding `?draft=` re-prefilled the chat input on every reload** — the deep link is consumed at mount and stripped from the URL.
- **A cleared search field could resurrect its query for 300 ms** — the debounced highlight term is forced empty the instant the input empties (found by the hook's own test).
- **`conversations↔journals` runtime cycle** — introduced by the first QW-5 design (lazy import of journals from conversations), caught by the F009 domain-cycle ratchet, resolved with the injected port + startup registration; cycles stay at 31/31 baseline.

### Changed

- **Streaming chunk accounting consolidated** — the four per-branch metric blocks became one `_track_and_observe` chokepoint (metric + trace capture), and the `_get_chunk_event_type` if/elif chain became a lookup table: `streaming/service.py` shrank back under its frozen SLOC cap while gaining the capture.
- **`ChatMessage` decomposed** — proactive token-field resolution and the feedback gate extracted as pure helpers; the frontend CC baseline was **lowered** (max 74 → 60) and locked in.
- **History rows always carry `message_db_id`** — `toUiMessage` mirrors the live done metadata so live and reloaded bubbles share one feedback contract (the mapping contract test was updated accordingly).

### Tests

- Backend: **+34 net (12,468 collected)** — trace capture (16: reset/seed, per-key dedup, cap keeps the tail, PII exclusions, defensive copies), resolver error-status (9: ERROR match, REVOKED ineligible, legacy alias, category mismatch, lookup failure never masks), connector notice V2 additions in the ADR-134 suite (enriched/plain classification, direct emission), the search contract rewritten on the real DB (accents both directions, literal wildcards), response feedback (6 integration on the real DB: first-verdict counters, verdict change never re-feeds, 👎 comment → L0, journals-disabled, ownership/404, foreign/vanished ids skipped). Suite: 10,644 unit-fast green, cycles 31/31, lint + MyPy strict clean.
- Frontend: **+63** — trace hydration (10), search hook state machine (10: debounce, availability gating, pagination, error, jump `+1 ms`, return, send guard), results panel (7), rehype highlighter (9) + MarkdownContent integration (4), actionable cards (4, role/name oracles), portrait hint/shortcut (8 + 2), feedback buttons (4), context-pill totals (3). Suite: 2 282 green, tsc/ESLint/Prettier clean, a11y/react-hooks ratchets at baseline, i18n parity ×6.
- Runtime, on the dev Docker stack (dedicated QA account, real login): a weather turn's archived row carries the 6-step trace and the reloaded browser bubble shows it expanded; a forged `status=ERROR` Gmail row makes a real email turn emit the `tool_error {google_gmail, reconnect}` SSE chunk; a real turn's `done` carries `archived_message_id`, the posted 👎+comment is reread from the API, a foreign id 404s — and the verdict flipped from the browser lands in the database with `response_feedback_total{verdict="thumbs_up"} 1.0` on `/metrics`.

## [1.25.11] - 2026-07-21

> **A widget that fails now says why — and the interactive map finally works everywhere.** Asked from an iPhone, the map was a blank rectangle: the app-wide `COEP: require-corp` (needed once for the voice wake-word's `SharedArrayBuffer`) is only lifted by the Chromium-only `credentialless` iframe attribute — WebKit cancels the embed with **no event, no message, no log**. Behind that one symptom, measurement found a family. Widget payloads lived only in the browser's React state, so a reload — or the other device — showed grey "unavailable" boxes. The LLM imitated host-owned widget markup from its own history: duplicate and phantom widgets, proven **byte-for-byte** in production data. The skill sub-agent had no notion of the user's position: _"montre-moi où je suis"_ sent the literal words _"ma position"_ — then _"France"_ — as Google Maps search queries, while the geolocation permission prompt never fired for that phrasing in any of the 6 languages. And the analyzer's skill detection hijacked MCP-domain turns three times in a row: a diagram request drew the water cycle **on a Google Maps embed**, then spawned a parasite skill whose failed import dumped inline SVG into the chat — the third attempt only reached Excalidraw because the hallucinated skill name did not exist. Five hypotheses were refuted by measurement on the way; a Playwright bench replayed the **real 450 kB production payload** through the **real airlock shell** on both engines, light and dark; and that same bench destroyed a design assumption before it shipped — `document.open()` erases the Window's listeners, so the boot-failure relay hooks are installed _after_ `document.close()`, not before. Also in this cycle, shipped on `main` between the two releases: the security wave (16 alerts, 7 advisories), 109 npm updates, the six founding ADRs reconstituted, and a 215-file documentation realignment.

### Added

- **`COEP_MODE` (default `credentialless`, ADR-136)** — `resolveCoepMode()` in `src/lib/csp.ts`, env-switchable without rebuild, falling back to the default on any unrecognized value (a typo must never silently drop cross-origin isolation). Chromium keeps isolation, `SharedArrayBuffer` and the wake-word; WebKit loses an isolation it could never combine with external embeds anyway and falls back to push-to-talk — a degradation `isSherpaKwsSupported()` already handled.
- **Widget failure states** — `canEmbedOpaqueCrossOriginFrame()` refuses to render an embed the engine will reject (on Chromium the refusal is otherwise _invisible_: `load` fires on the error document); `useFrameLoadWatchdog` turns a dead frame into an actionable card (message, retry, navigable link) after `NEXT_PUBLIC_WIDGET_FRAME_TIMEOUT_MS`. Liveness is per family: a skill frame's document IS the widget (`load` suffices), an MCP App only proves itself by speaking the protocol (`ui/initialize` handshake) — the airlock shell always loads, so `load` says nothing there. The MCP notice is deliberately **non-destructive**: it renders above the frame, which stays mounted, and a late handshake clears it.
- **Airlock boot-failure relay (ADR-136)** — the shell installs `error` (capture phase — resource failures don't bubble) and `unhandledrejection` hooks after writing the widget document, and relays up to 5 length-capped `lia:widget-error` messages to the parent. The timeout notice shows the detail as **plain text only** (`mcp_apps.frame_error_detail`, 6 languages): a phone report now names the culprit — _"Widget script failed — its CDN imports may be unreachable"_ — without a Mac attached to it. Measured on both engines: an inline module whose static import fails emits an event with no message and no src, so the shell names the likeliest suspect itself.
- **Widgets travel with their message (ADR-137)** — `SKILL_APP`/`MCP_APP` payloads are persisted in `message_metadata.widgets` at archive time and rehydrated on history reads, merged _under_ the live registry. `DRAFT` is deliberately excluded (stale HITL state must not invite confirming an action the graph no longer knows). The per-widget budget is **measured, not estimated**: the first 64 kB figure was 7× too small — production logged a 473 kB Excalidraw payload — and is now 1 MB. Rehydating from the LangGraph checkpoint was rejected by measurement (LRU-capped registry, ~70/75 slots already used in production).
- **`is_system_skill` recomputed at read time, per user** — the flag grants `credentialless` + `allow-same-origin` and is never trusted from a persisted payload. `SkillsCache.entry_is_system` / `get_system_skill_names(user_id)` are the single predicate (`scope == "admin"`, the exact expression the DB sync already used), with the same override semantics as the write path: a user skill shadowing a system name must not have its widget re-promoted — a hole found by counter-review and pinned by test before it shipped.
- **Host-owned widget sentinels (ADR-137)** — `display/sentinel_filter.py` strips LLM-authored sentinel copies with `html.parser` (never a regex: sentinels nest `<div>`s) at three chokepoints: before canonical injection, in the ReAct history window (replaced by a placeholder — the imitation _prompt_ disappears and the tokens come back), and on the ReAct passthrough. `widget_sentinels_stripped_total{source}` tells whether the model still imitates instead of assuming it. Invariant pinned by test: N interactive widgets ⇔ N sentinels, proven non-vacuous by re-injecting the production duplicate.
- **User location for the skill runner** — `services/skill_location_context.py` resolves the position through the same `resolve_location()` chokepoint every location-aware tool uses (browser geolocation first, then home address) and feeds the versioned prompt's new `{user_location}` variable as a language-free `"lat,lon"` value; all wording lives in the prompt file, and the `"unknown"` sentinel coupling is pinned by test.
- **`frame.link_url` in the `SkillScriptOutput` contract** — the _user-facing_ URL for the fallback card, https-enforced like `url`. The Google Maps embed endpoint answers _"must be used in an iframe"_ when opened top-level; `render_map.py` now ships `google.com/maps?q=…` alongside it, and both fallbacks prefer it.
- **QUERY location phrases in both mirrors (6 languages)** — the frontend detector had no "where am I" category at all (backend had it, minus the imperative forms), so _"montre-moi où je suis"_ never triggered the just-in-time geolocation permission prompt. Both tables gain the imperative forms (`"où je suis"`, `"ma position"`, `"where i am"`, `"wo ich bin"`), and `GeolocationPrompt` reacts to the new category.
- **MCP-domain guard** (`services/analysis/skill_suppression.py`) — the analyzer LLM fills `domains` and `skill_name` in one output with no coherence guarantee, and the routing decider gave the skill absolute priority. The guard suppresses the detection when the _primary_ domain is an MCP domain, reusing the exact ADR-118 dialogue exemption the chat override applies (a mid-dialogue conversational answer keeps its dialogue skill; a fresh imperative request does not). Every suppression is logged and counted (`skill_detection_suppressed_total{reason}`).

### Fixed

- **Interactive map blank on every iOS browser** — `require-corp` + no `credentialless` in WebKit; verbatim engine message: _"Cancelled load … because it violates the resource's Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy response header"_. Root-caused on a Playwright bench with production headers replicated, engine × header matrix measured.
- **Widgets lost on reload or on the other device** — payloads were fed exclusively by the live SSE stream; verified in production: `message_metadata` carried only `run_id`/`intention`/`psyche_state`, and rendering real production content against an empty registry produced two grey error boxes and zero iframes.
- **Duplicate and phantom widgets** — production message `28eaa427` carried the same `data-registry-id` twice (two iframes mounted, byte-arithmetic reconciled to the stored length); two later replies embedded sentinels the backend never injected, pointing at a dead turn — one of them said "I don't have access to your position" _while displaying a map_.
- **Rehydrated widgets demoted on desktop** — the history filter read `is_system` on SkillsCache entries that only carry `scope` (the key exists only on the SQL table), so the system-skill set was always empty, every rehydrated frame lost its privileges, and the embed probe refused it ("Open in a browser"). The write path carried the same confusion with a permissive `True` default — a latent privilege escalation for user-imported skills, closed in the same change.
- **"Montre-moi où je suis" answered with maps of "ma position" and France** — the skill-bypass plan is empty (no tool runs, no collected data) and the sub-agent's four tools cannot resolve a position, so the model improvised search strings; it also ran the successful script twice (two widgets: the ADR-137 invariant faithfully rendered a double execution) and shipped its deliberation as the visible reply. The prompt now makes a successful script FINAL and the final message VERBATIM.
- **`resolve_location` silently dropped `LocationType.QUERY`** — the match had no branch for it, so "où suis-je" fell through to the "unreachable" `(None, None)`: no location _and_ no user-facing hint.
- **Diagram requests hijacked away from Excalidraw** — three consecutive production turns with `primary_domain=mcp_excalidraw` at 0.95 confidence were routed to `interactive-map`, then `skill-generator`, then a hallucinated `"mcp_excalidraw"` skill; only the third reached the MCP task, and only because the bypass failed on the non-existent name.
- **Dead fallback link** — "Open in a browser" opened the embed-only `frame_url`, which Google refuses top-level.
- **`react_result` dual-shape crash** — the state contract dict and the runner dataclass shared one `Any`-typed name; production run `117ce96f` died on `AttributeError: 'ReactSubAgentResult' object has no attribute 'get'`, collapsing the turn to a 98-character fallback. The runner branch now normalizes onto the single state contract, and the three annotations are `dict[str, Any] | None`.
- **Cross-turn skill-skip guard** — `_plan_already_produced_skill_app` scanned every past turn's results against a docstring that promised "the same turn": a widget produced at turn 47 silently suppressed the runner at every later turn (production run `d0fad28b`). Now scoped to the `{turn_id}:` prefix.
- **MCP frames rendered as a black slab in dark mode** — the iframe background was `--lia-bg`; an empty widget now shows the page through (`transparent`), on both widget families.
- **`Context type 'mcps' not registered` error-logged on every MCP tool result** — MCP manifests claimed `context_key="mcps"`, a context type that was never registered (MCP result shapes are heterogeneous per server), so the wave auto-save attempted a doomed save and error-logged it; the noise surfaced as soon as the MCP-domain guard let those turns reach the pipeline. The manifests now carry no `context_key` (the executor's designed no-context path); `"mcps"` keeps its display role (result cards, registry items) untouched.

- **`browser_screenshot_card_url` — SSE stream killed one statement before `done`** (CodeQL `py/uninitialized-local-variable`, the only `error`-level alert). Declared inside the `elif response_content.strip():` archive branch but read two levels up, in the done-metadata block. An assistant reply that streams no content skips that branch — there is no `else` — while the `if not hitl_interrupt_detected` guard above the read still passes. Declared next to `archived_assistant_msg_id`, at the level it is read from.
- **`interaction` — the HITL fallback crashed the request it was meant to rescue** (not reported by CodeQL; found with pyright). Assigned by the first statement of a `try` and read by that same try's handler, whose `except (AttributeError, KeyError, ValueError, RuntimeError)` does not catch `NameError`. Both `from_action_type` call sites take the same arguments, so a failure in one implies a failure in the other — the sentinel is declared ahead of both, and the handler now treats `None` explicitly via `suppress`.
- **Truncated `<style>`/`<script>` blocks leaked their raw body as prose**, on _both_ halves of the notification pipeline (`js/bad-tag-filter` on the frontend; invisible on the backend, where `py/bad-tag-filter` is excluded by config — the backend defect was established by executing both implementations, not assumed). These surfaces truncate, so a severed `<style>` keeps no `</style>`: tag-stripping removed the marker and a lock screen read `body{color:red;font-size:12px}`. The closing tag is now optional on both sides, with `(?<!/)` so a self-closing `<script src="x"/>` cannot swallow the document and a `\1` backreference so a `</script>` cannot close a `<style>`. Not an XSS on either side: output feeds escaped React children only.
- **FAQ `voice_mode` section rendered none of its six answers** — the key was absent from the section wiring in `FAQContent.tsx`.
- **A long conversation opened mid-history.** The component does not own its scrolling box (`scrollHeight === clientHeight` on its own node, so every `scrollTop` write is a no-op), and content keeps growing after first paint. `getScrollParent()` resolves the real scroller and the viewport is re-pinned for a 1500 ms window.

### Security

**The alert dashboard was not the perimeter.** A review of 15 code-scanning alerts and 5 advisories found **16 and 7** — and the two defects that actually broke behaviour were neither the `critical` nor the `high` ones. Alert #844 appeared mid-review, on code shipped the day before. Two advisories (`brace-expansion`, `js-yaml`) were in no dashboard at all — the first because _our own override_ pinned a vulnerable version. And a second `UnboundLocalError`, never reported by CodeQL, was found by auditing the class with a tool that could actually see it. What let this accumulate was a single flag: `pnpm audit` ran with `continue-on-error: true`, so a CRITICAL advisory lived on `main` for months under a green pipeline.

- **`pnpm audit` is blocking again** — `continue-on-error: true` removed from `security.yml`. That flag is how `websocket-driver` GHSA-xv26-6w52-cph6 (critical) survived on `main` under a green pipeline.
- **5 advisories patched via `pnpm.overrides`**: `websocket-driver` 0.7.4 → 0.7.5 (critical + moderate; production dependency via firebase but unreachable — only `firebase/app` and `firebase/messaging` are imported), `minimatch` 9.0.5 → 9.0.9 (3 high ReDoS, scoped `minimatch@9` so ESLint's 3.1.5 is untouched), `brace-expansion` → `^2.0.3` (our own override pinned the vulnerable 2.0.2), `js-yaml` → `^4.2.0`. `pnpm audit` goes from 5 findings to 1 low (dev-only, not executed).
- **CodeQL analysed every frontend test directory** — `**/tests/**` does not match `__tests__`, so 31 directories were scanned despite the stated intent, the origin of 9 of the 16 alerts. `**/__tests__/**` is now listed explicitly.
- **`SecuritySettings.algorithm` constrained to `Literal["HS256","HS384","HS512"]`.** The `CVE-2024-23342` pip-audit exemption claimed LIA "only verifies JWTs" — it signs them; what makes the ecdsa timing attack inert is HS256. `ALGORITHM` being a documented `.env` knob, the Literal is what stops a configuration change from silently invalidating a security exemption.
- **`lia_gender` cookie** gains `SameSite=Lax` and a protocol-conditional `Secure` (unconditional would drop it on a plain-HTTP dev origin).
- **`pyasn1` 0.6.3 → 0.6.4** (CVE-2026-59886, DoS via ASN.1 REAL float conversion) — the advisory landed the day of the release and the now-blocking `pip-audit` gate caught it before the tag went out: the flag removed in this very cycle did exactly what it exists for.

### Changed

- **The ReAct history window serves widget placeholders instead of raw sentinel markup** — the model no longer sees the pattern it was imitating, and the tokens the markup consumed come back.
- **The skill-runner prompt hardened** (versioned `skill_react_agent_prompt`) — a successful `run_skill_script` is FINAL (never re-run to "improve" a result; retry only after an explicit error, once), placeholder location strings are forbidden when `UserLocation` is `"unknown"`, and the final message is displayed VERBATIM (no narrated reasoning).
- **`widget_persist_max_bytes` default recalibrated 64 kB → 1 MB** — the original figure was reasoned from skill frames alone; production measured a 473 kB MCP widget being dropped, which resurfaced as "erreur de chargement de l'application" on every reload.
- **109 npm minor/patch updates**, with the root `vite` override realigned to 8.1.5. Dependabot does not read workspace-root overrides when bumping a workspace member, so its PR contradicted the override and could never pass `--frozen-lockfile` — a rebase clears the git conflict without fixing that.
- **6 GitHub Actions updated** (SHA-pinned).
- **`IntersectionObserver` test stub takes real constructor arguments** — 7 `js/superfluous-trailing-arguments` alerts came from CodeQL resolving the global to a stub with no constructor. The dropped callback is why `ChatMessageList.test.tsx` had to ship its own observer double. The `as unknown as` double cast is gone.

### Removed

- **8 dead `GuideLayout` exports** (`GuideSection`, `GuideSubSection`, `GuideP`, `GuideBold`, `GuideQuote`, `GuideTable`, `GuideList`, `GuideCode`) — `GuideToc` was the only one consumed.
- **A dead `return` in `rag_spaces/processing.py`** whose comment claimed mypy needed it for totality; mypy is clean without it.

#### Full documentation realignment (215 files audited, ADRs excluded)

Eight mechanically verifiable classes were audited with purpose-built detectors.
**Five of the eight detectors were wrong on first run** and were fixed before any
edit — one ignored the `apps/api/src/` prefix (136 false positives), one matched the
word "task" inside prose, one counted `node_exporter` metrics as ours, one confused
settings with metrics, one missed FastAPI's multi-line decorators, one never read the
"Tables complémentaires" section. Acting on their first output would have "fixed" a
sound codebase. Each was validated against a known-true case, and every correction
re-measured afterwards.

**Operationally dangerous defects — they mislead during an incident:**

- **`RedisConnectionPoolExhaustion.md`** instructed operators to edit
  `REDIS_POOL_SIZE`, `REDIS_POOL_MAX_OVERFLOW` and five more variables **that do not

  `pkce_validation_failures_total` where the rule reads

  `AgentsStreamingErrorRateHigh`. A wrong PromQL name returns nothing, **silently**.
- **`AgentsRouterLatencyHigh.md`** told operators to change `ROUTER_MODEL` in `.env`;
  models live in the database (`LLM_TYPES_REGISTRY`), and no such variable exists.

  encrypted `provider_api_keys` table has been the sole source of truth since

- **`SCHEDULED_ACTIONS_ENABLED` does not exist** — yet **`CLAUDE.md`** listed it among
  the feature flags, and two guides documented it. Scheduled actions are always wired.
- **~25 phantom environment variables** corrected or flagged: `HEARTBEAT_*` (4 wrong
  names), `MCP_EXCALIDRAW_*` (5, never implemented), Langfuse "Phase 3.1" features (3,

  `MCP_APPS_MAX_HTML_SIZE` → `MCP_APP_MAX_HTML_SIZE` (singular), `ROUTER/PLANNER_MESSAGE_WINDOW_SIZE`,
  `VOICE_WAKE_WORD_ENABLED`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT`.
  `DATABASE_URL_SYNC` was documented as settable — it is a computed property.

**API routes — 25 corrections.** `GET /users/me` → `/auth/me`; `PATCH /users/me` →
`/users/{user_id}`; `/conversations/history` → `/conversations/me/messages`;

`/app/call-tool`; `/admin/mcp/servers` → `/mcp/servers`. Three endpoints do not exist at

`langgraph_agent_node_duration_seconds` → `langgraph_stage_duration_seconds`,

Mocks must carry the public attributes of what they replace.
