## [1.25.1] - 2026-07-16

> **Security hardening — audit Lot 1 remediation, transparent and zero-regression.** First wave of fixes from an independent security audit conducted on 2026-07-13. Every finding was verified against the real code before remediation (no material false positive); **no feature was removed** — each fix is a pure reinforcement shipped with tests and an executable anti-recurrence guard. Verified: Ruff + Black + MyPy strict + tsc + ESLint clean, 10,188 backend unit + 1,278 vitest + 27/27 hermetic deploy tests green, disclosure endpoint served live.

### Security

- **SEC-012 — credentials no longer reach the logs.** The central structlog PII
  filter now pseudonymizes opaque OAuth `state`/CSRF tokens (correlatable, non
  reversible), strips the values of sensitive URL query parameters
  (`?token=`/`?code=`/…) from any logged link, and redacts PKCE/`client_secret`/
  `id_token` fields — covering all ~34 `state=` log sites systemically. The
  verification/reset email logs also stop passing the signed URL (defense in
  depth). Guard: behavioral tests in `test_pii_filter.py`.
- **SEC-017 — RAG upload route-escape closed.** `apps/web/.../rag-upload/[spaceId]`
  rejects any non-UUID `spaceId` with `400` before reading the body or building
  the upstream URL, so an encoded `..%2f…` can no longer retarget another
  backend route. Guard: `route.test.ts` (no upstream request on rejection).
- **SEC-022 — version drift removed.** The root endpoint and OpenAPI schema now
  advertise the release version (`settings.app_version`) distinctly from the
  stable `/v1` API-contract constant, instead of a single confusing `1.0.0`.
  Guard: `test_version_consistency_guard.py`.
- **SEC-023 — working disclosure channel.** Added an RFC 9116
  `/.well-known/security.txt` and rewrote `SECURITY.md` to correct the supported
  versions (`1.x`), route reports to GitHub Security Advisories, and drop
  unverified control claims. Guard: `test_security_disclosure_guard.py`
  (future `Expires`, no dead domain / fictitious versions).
- **SEC-025 — HSTS on the frontend.** The public HTTPS responses now carry
  `Strict-Transport-Security` in production (env-tunable `HSTS_MAX_AGE`, starting
  short, without `includeSubDomains`/`preload`). Guard: `csp.test.ts`.
- **SEC-013 — production `.env` permissions hardened.** The deploy driver enforces
  `0600` on the remote `.env` inside a `0700` directory (plus the Claude CLI
  credentials) right before `docker compose up`. Guard: hermetic Pester test in
  `deploy-prod.Tests.ps1`.

## [1.25.0] - 2026-07-16

> **Audit V11 — fully revised framework, register cleared, and a test/CI foundation hardened at the root.** The technical audit moved to a **normalized framework**: 24 areas mapped to **ISO/IEC 25010:2023**, evaluated under **ISO/IEC 25040:2024** (architecture per ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022, test processes per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-2:2021, structural quality per ISO/IEC 5055:2021, accessibility controlled against **WCAG 2.2 AA**), each score backed by **at least three executed evidence points**, a dedicated counter-analysis of false positives/negatives, and a plain arithmetic mean — **8.3/10 (199/240)**, security explicitly out of scope. Scores are **not comparable** with the pre-revision grid (8.5/10): the framework got stricter, and this very release closed **every previously-open major and minor finding** — the register now holds **7 moderate worksites (AC-001…AC-007), 0 major, 0 minor**, each published with evidence, closure criteria, effort and a ready-to-run resolution prompt. Full standalone report versioned at `docs/audit/AUDIT_CODEBASE_2026-07-16_CONSOLIDE_V11.html`; public summary and revised protocol in `docs/audit/`.

### Added

- **Audit V11 publication** — standalone HTML report (opinion, 24-area scorecard, executed-evidence register, positive controls, worksites with AI resolution prompts, counter-analysis, prioritization horizons, annexes) + rewritten public summary (`docs/audit/README.md`) + `AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md` aligned on the revised framework (anchored 0.5-step scale, arithmetic mean over 24 normalized areas, AC-numbered findings with major/moderate/minor levels and E1–E5 efforts, counter-analysis stage, dated referentials incl. WCAG 2.2).
- **Process-wide test-database redirection** (`tests/conftest.py::_redirect_process_db`) — integration tests now redirect _every_ DB entrypoint (settings, the module-level engine behind `get_db_context()`/`get_db_session()`, the LangGraph checkpointer & store pools via a new injectable `psycopg_pool_config` helper) to the test database, with a `DevDatabaseAccessError` guard that fails loudly on any developer-DB connection while Testcontainers is active. Contracts pinned in `test_db_redirection_contract.py` + `test_psycopg_pool_contract.py`.
- **Session-scoped LangGraph table provisioning** (`_provision_langgraph_tables`) — the checkpointer/store `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` migrations run once per session via the sync savers, when no test transaction is open; in-test `setup()` becomes a version check. Kills a whole-run freeze (server-side DDL deadlock against the per-test outer transaction) — regression pinned by a bounded test proven red/green.
- **Launcher-environment isolation** — `tests/conftest.py` scrubs every key declared in the repo-root `.env` before loading `.env.test`: the task runner's `dotenv: [.env]` no longer leaks the developer environment into test processes (observed: a ships-dark semantic-expansion flag rerouting 7 tests; `DEFAULT_CURRENCY=EUR` + a real currency API converting cost assertions at the **live** exchange rate). Contract proven red under simulated contamination (`test_env_isolation_contract.py`); shared pricing/semantic caches also reset around every test (`test_state_reset_contract.py`).
- **Testcontainers on Windows, at full speed** — `tc_host_override` forced to IPv4 loopback automatically (no manual env var) + URL normalization: the ~30× slow doomed-IPv6-first path is gone (measured 105.8 s → 3.5 s for 2 DB tests). Contract tests hold on Linux CI too.
- **`DATABASE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`** setting — libpq/psycopg connection-establishment bound on the LangGraph pools (defense in depth against stalled TCP handshakes on freshly published Docker ports), shared through the new `psycopg_pool_config` helper (DRY conninfo + kwargs for checkpointer and store).
- **E2E dashboard-shell mocks** (`apps/web/e2e/fixtures/dashboard-shell.ts`) — 9 type-correct endpoint mocks (config, personalities, connector health, psyche, usage limits, voice ticket, RAG spaces) installed by `authenticate` under spec-level mocks; the 501 catch-all still fails any undeclared call loudly. The voice ticket deliberately answers 403 — a granted ticket opens a real WebSocket that Playwright cannot intercept and retry-storms the dev server.

### Changed

- **E2E proof runs target a production standalone server** — the managed CI web server now does `next build` → copy `.next/static` + `public/` into the standalone tree (same layout as `Dockerfile.prod`) → `node .next/standalone/apps/web/server.js` (`next start` does not work with `output: standalone`); local proof recipe documented (`NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-e2e` next.config parameter so the build coexists with the running dev server; `NODE_ENV=production` required; `127.0.0.1` targets — the standalone server binds IPv4-only). Dev-server runs keep `workers: 1` (parallel on-demand compilation corrupts the webpack cache) and `a11y/scan.ts` now waits for the design-system tokens before any axe scan, aborting with an actionable error on an unstyled page — a degraded server can no longer produce phantom WCAG violations (the reported dark-mode `#9e9eff`-on-white "defect" was exactly that artifact; the dark palette is proven clean, **17/17 E2E including dark mode**).
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=""` is preserved** — five `||` fallbacks (including the root `env:` block of `next.config.ts`, inlined into the whole bundle) became `??`: an explicit empty string means same-origin relative `/api/v1` URLs through the BFF proxy (hermetic CI builds), only a truly absent variable gets the dev fallback. Contract proven red/green (`api-base-url-env.test.ts`).
- **Unit-suite network guard hardened** — `UnitTestNetworkError` now subclasses `OSError` so `socket.create_connection` callers close their just-created socket (the RuntimeError variant leaked sockets into `PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning` false-greens); real loopback I/O opened during an async unit test is closed on the test's own loop; `error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning` is a permanent hard gate.
- **Redis injection seams** — `PlanPatternLearner` and `KnowledgeEnrichmentService` take a `RedisProvider` constructor seam (client never cached on the singleton — `close_redis()` resets are honored); the shared rate limiter rebuilds its wrapper when the client identity changes. Isolation proven against a dead Redis port.

### Fixed

- **Windows integration bootstrap** — `caldav → niquests → urllib3-future` clobbered `urllib3` via a wheel overwrite plus a `.pth` re-clobbering every Python start, breaking docker-py/testcontainers on Windows (420+ silent skips reading as green). The editor opt-out (`URLLIB3_NO_OVERRIDE=1` + `--no-binary urllib3-future`) is encoded on all four install surfaces (Taskfile, Dockerfile.dev, Dockerfile.prod, CI), guarded by a namespace test, and `task test:backend:integration` gets an actionable DB-strategy preflight + `LIA_REQUIRE_DB=1` so mass skips can never fake green again.
- **Fresh-install production build** — `markdown-sanitize-schema.ts` imported `defaultSchema` from the undeclared transitive `hast-util-sanitize` (masked by hoisted local node_modules; `Module not found` on `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`); switched to the official `rehype-sanitize@6` re-export, XSS pipeline byte-identical (38/38 sanitize/math tests).
- **15 obsolete permanent skips reactivated** — 7 Windows `skipif` (psycopg SelectorEventLoop is provided by the suite), 4 "checkpoint tables missing" (now provisioned), and 4 realigned on current contracts: PKCE authorization-URL assertions (S256 challenge, state echo, `redirect_uri` from settings), page-scoped `total_count`, reset-preserves-conversation (no soft delete), and invocation-boundary metrics callbacks (`enrich_config_with_node_metadata`). The main integration phase passes **579/579 with zero skips**; the skip allowlist shrank by 6 entries.
- **WCAG dark-mode false alarm** — the audited `#9e9eff` on `#ffffff` contrast failures were Chromium UA link colors on an unstyled page served by a degraded dev server (identical color pair across different design tokens — impossible for a real palette). No palette change was needed; the scan guard prevents recurrence.

### Tests

- Full campaign green at the audited snapshot: **~10,150 fast unit** (unraisable-exception hard gate), **972 agents**, **579 integration with zero skips** (Windows + Testcontainers, ~3.5 min), **1,222 vitest**, **17/17 Playwright E2E** against the standalone production build (axe blocking, dark mode, 320 px reflow, 200% zoom, keyboard), Alembic empty-DB replay, deployment harness 25/25, both production images built. New contracts: DB redirection (9), psycopg pool lifecycle, env isolation (2+2 red/green), testcontainers IPv4 (9+2), base-URL semantics (5), urllib3 namespace (4).

## [1.24.0] - 2026-07-13

> **Agentic telephony** — LIA can now place an outbound phone call on your behalf, hold a goal-directed, **read-only** conversation with a third party (e.g. check a contact's availability, pass along a message), and report back **asynchronously** in the chat with a summary and an optional one-click follow-up. Modeled as a **per-user connector** (Préférences → Mes Connecteurs) with full BYO: each user brings their own ElevenLabs API key + imported number, and calls are billed on their own accounts (no LIA-side cost metering — D-9). The whole flow reuses the existing **draft/HITL** machinery (you confirm the call before it dials) and the proactive-notification delivery. **Data protection is by capability, not by prompt**: the agent only ever receives a pre-fetched, minimized **free/busy** projection (busy time ranges only, never meeting titles/attendees/locations), so it physically cannot leak what it was never given; recording is disabled at the vendor API and the raw transcript is never persisted — only a minimized, expiring summary. Feature-flagged (`TELEPHONY_ENABLED`, **off by default**), 6 languages. Architecture: ADR-127; technical reference: `docs/technical/TELEPHONY.md`. Written à blanc against the documented ElevenLabs Agents API — the exact vendor request/response shapes are `spike:`-flagged and gated on a real ElevenLabs + Twilio account before go-live; every external-payload read is defensive. Dormant until activated — no impact on any existing feature, no DB migration to an existing table.

### Added

- **Agentic telephony connector** (`ELEVENLABS_TELEPHONY`, `apps/api/src/domains/telephony/`) — per-user BYO activation wizard (validate ElevenLabs key → pick a workspace number → configure the post-call webhook → provision a guardrailed LIA agent). API key + webhook HMAC secret stored **encrypted** in `credentials_encrypted` (never in JSONB); only non-secret ids in `connector_metadata`. Frontend wizard in _Préférences → Mes Connecteurs_ (`TelephonyConnectorForm`, `useTelephony`) + a call-history surface that omits the phone number.
- **`place_phone_call` draft tool + `DraftType.PHONE_CALL`** — resolves the callee (a raw international number is used as-is; a name is resolved against the active contacts provider), then produces an HITL draft (`draft_critique` → `draft_executor`) so you confirm callee + objective before LIA dials. Display registry + preview renderer + i18n (noun `call` / verb `placed`, 6 languages with gender agreement) guarded by a boot-time completeness assert (ADR-085 pattern).
- **Availability pre-fetch** (`availability.py`) — a minimized **free/busy** projection over the active calendar (`fields=["start","end"]` → busy ranges only), injected as the agent's `{{availability_summary}}` dynamic variable. Meeting details are never even fetched.
- **Post-call return path** — an unauthenticated `POST /telephony/webhook` with **foreign-filter → per-user HMAC verification** (Stripe-style timestamped signature, replay window) → fire-and-forget reconciliation; a single **tool-less** LLM call (`telephony_synthesis` type + versioned prompt, structured output) produces a factual summary + first-person proposal, delivered via `NotificationDispatcher`. Exactly-once via an atomic conditional UPDATE; one-active-call-per-user via a partial unique index.
- **Background reapers** — stale-call recovery (interval) + retention purge (daily, clears summary/structured_data past their TTL) registered in the scheduler; `GET /telephony/calls`.
- **Observability** — Prometheus `telephony_calls_total{status}`, `telephony_call_duration_seconds`, `telephony_webhook_ignored_total{reason}`; the synthesis LLM call's tokens are tracked via `track_proactive_tokens` (task type `phone_call`), consistent with briefing/heartbeat.
- **ADR-127** (Agentic Telephony) + `docs/technical/TELEPHONY.md` (architecture, security invariants, §17 setup runbook, spike list), cross-referenced in `docs/INDEX.md` + `docs/architecture/ADR_INDEX.md`.

### Changed

- All telephony backend strings centralized in `src/core/i18n_telephony.py` (6 languages, typed accessors); the ElevenLabs agent guardrail system prompt moved to the versioned `prompts/v1/telephony_agent_system_prompt.txt`. New `telephony_synthesis` LLM type in `LLM_TYPES_REGISTRY` + `LLM_DEFAULTS` + the factory `LLMType` literal + admin-UI description (6 languages).

### Fixed

- **Pre-release hardening** (caught by adversarial review of the à-blanc code, never shipped): crash-safe dial — the `dialing` row is committed **before** the vendor call and the DB transaction is never held across an external HTTP call, so a crash after dialing can't orphan a call whose post-call webhook could never reconcile; the `place_phone_call` draft factory was extracted to the telephony bounded context to keep the shared drafts service under the file-size ratchet; defensive structured-data extraction with the `ValidationError` logged by type only (never the offending value → no PII at WARNING).

### Tests

- **100+ backend unit tests + 8 integration tests on real PostgreSQL** (the F12 one-active-call partial index, `mark_completed` exactly-once, `recover_stale`/`purge_expired`, connector activation) — the `Enum(native_enum=False)` name/value predicate proven against Postgres in UPDATEs. Frontend: 6 `useTelephony` vitest tests. Contract test pins the agent's collected fields to `StructuredCallData`. File-size ratchet + black/ruff/mypy clean; i18n parity across the 6 locales; dev container boots healthy.

## [1.23.13] - 2026-07-11

> Companion presence, embodiment micro-interactions, and a documentation realignment. LIA gains a **floating mini-avatar** that follows across the dashboard (everywhere except chat, where the real avatar already lives) — resting as the current mood, "thinking" while a background run is active, badged when notifications are unread, minimizable to a dot. Around it, three grounded touches make the interface feel alive without decoration: a **time-aware empty-chat greeting**, a **proactive-notification avatar wobble** (live arrival only, never on history), and a **"just updated ✨" freshness badge** on briefing cards. The mood-colored bubble glow shipped in v1.23.12 was **retired** on user judgment after UAT. The release also folds in an already-landed documentation realignment (236 broken doc links → 0) and two dev-hygiene items (a committed `doc_audit.py` drift instrument, an infra-denylist false-positive fix). Every animation degrades to the previous behavior on asset failure, hidden psyche visuals, and `prefers-reduced-motion`. A real SSE reconnect-storm bug (inline callback identity) was found by driving the app end-to-end in the dev container and fixed. No backend feature change, no DB migration, no new dependency.

### Added

- **Companion presence** (`components/companion/CompanionPresence.tsx`, mounted in the dashboard layout) — a floating LIA mini-avatar on every dashboard page **except chat** (hidden there, where it also disables its SSE + polling so exactly one notifications connection is ever active). Three grounded states: **rest** (mood `AnimatedEmoji`, gentle float; classic "LIA" badge when psyche is off), **working** (a small `TypingIndicator` bubble driven by a gentle `GET /agents/runs/active` poll — ADR-117), and a **notification** count badge fed by a layout-level `useNotifications` subscription with a one-shot attention wobble on live arrival. Click → chat (and clears the badge); minimize → a discreet restore dot (session-scoped, never permanently hidden). Pure reuse of `AssistantAvatar` / `TypingIndicator` / `useNotifications` / `fetchActiveRun`.
- **Time-aware empty-chat greeting** — the hero emoji follows the user's local hour: ☕ morning (05–10), 👋 day (11–17), 🌛 evening (18–22), 😴 deep night (23–04), the last with a truthful "at night, LIA consolidates its memories" note grounded in the real nightly `memory_consolidation` / `memory_cleanup` jobs. Rendered through `AnimatedEmoji` (static-glyph fallback), behind a `mounted` gate that prevents any SSR hydration mismatch. New assets ☕/🌛/😴; one i18n key ×6.
- **Proactive-notification avatar wobble** — when a proactive/reminder/subagent/scheduled notification arrives **live** (freshness guard on the message timestamp, ±10 s), the assistant avatar plays a one-shot `lia-bell-ring`; history-loaded rows never wobble.
- **Briefing freshness badge** — the dormant `UpdatedAtBadge.showJustUpdated` ("mis à jour ✨") is now wired: a completed card refresh (`isRefreshing` true→false) lights it for ~1.6 s.
- **`scripts/audit/doc_audit.py`** — committed documentation-drift instrument: broken relative links + stale code-path references across `docs/`, classified LIVING / HISTORICAL / ROADMAP, exiting non-zero on any LIVING broken link; wired into `AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md` as a mandatory pre-publication step.

### Changed

- **Full documentation & schema realignment against v1.23.12** — 236 broken relative links driven to 0 across `docs/`, stale code-path references corrected, Mermaid schemas re-synced with the code (103 files).

### Removed

- **Mood-colored glow on the streaming bubble** (v1.23.12 W2) — retired on user judgment after UAT ("inutile et inesthétique"). The `.mood-glow` rule, its `--mood-color` wiring in `ChatMessage`, the 3 tests, and every showcase mention across the 6 locales were removed; particles, mood ping, cross-fade, living weather, landing mockup and the animated milestone toast are untouched.

### Fixed

- **Companion notification SSE reconnect storm** — an inline `onNotification` callback changed identity every render, making `useNotifications` tear down and rebuild its `EventSource` continuously (~200 requests). Stabilized with `useCallback`; the badge also now clears when the user reaches chat by any route, not only by clicking the companion. (Found by driving the app end-to-end, not by unit tests.)
- **Companion → chat navigation on clean (locale-less) URLs** — naive `pathname.split('/')[1]` locale extraction produced a malformed target; now reuses the layout's `getLanguageFromPath` / `buildLocalizedPath`, guarded by a regression test.
- **Infra-denylist pre-commit false positives** — byte coincidences inside regenerated binary assets (Mermaid PNG renders) matched short denylist tokens and aborted legitimate commits; `grep -I` now skips binary files.

### Tests

- **+13 frontend tests** — `greetingForHour` buckets, `isFreshProactive` window, companion helpers (`isChatRoute`, `deriveCompanionState`, `companionChatHref` incl. the clean-URL regression). Full suite green: 523 tests / 50 files, ESLint + `tsc --noEmit` clean, i18n parity ×6, and the four frontend features runtime-verified in the dev container (greeting emoji + no hydration warning, briefing badge cycle, companion rest / hidden-on-chat / click / minimize).

## [1.23.12] - 2026-07-11

> The wow batch — six targeted effects that push the living interface (v1.23.10) one notch further, selected for their delight-to-cost ratio. The psyche gains its strongest embodiment yet: the actively streaming bubble takes a thin border and soft halo **in LIA's current mood color**, and a whitelisted strong emotion (intensity ≥ 80 %) releases a one-shot burst of three particles from the avatar — rarity is the point. The moment LIA starts answering becomes cinematic (the execution steps cross-fade into the first tokens instead of being sharply replaced), the dormant weather keyframes finally come alive on the Today Briefing card, and the landing's hero conversation mockup is upgraded to product level — live breathing steps and a transient streaming caret, so visitors see the real thing. Same discipline as the parent batch: pure frontend, zero dependency, hard fallbacks, reduced-motion covered (with two cascade-level traps caught in self-review: CSS animation shorthands never share an element, and fill-mode animations are neutralized by duration, not `animation: none`).

### Added

- **Mood glow (chat)** — the assistant bubble being streamed carries `border-color` + halo driven by a `--mood-color` CSS variable (resolved from the same psyche snapshot as the avatar); double-class specificity so the glow survives the bubble's own hover styles; background-color kept in the transition list to preserve hover timing. Psyche gate respected; regular border the instant the stream completes.
- **Rare emotion particles (psyche)** — a change-only, never-on-mount burst of 3 rising particles when the live avatar's active emotion switches to a whitelisted one (✨ joy, 🌟 wonder/pride, ❤️ tenderness, 💖 gratitude, ⚡ enthusiasm, 💢 frustration) at intensity ≥ 0.8. History rows and reduced-motion never burst; particles are `opacity: 0` at rest so a disabled animation leaves nothing frozen.
- **Progress → answer cross-fade (chat)** — the markdown wrapper of the active message is keyed on the reducer's `streaming.phase`: exactly one remount per response (none per token, none at stream end, none on history), playing a 300 ms fade when the first real tokens replace the execution steps.
- **Living weather (Today Briefing)** — the dormant `lia-rain-drop` / `lia-sun-rays` keyframes are finally wired: falling 💧 on Rain/Drizzle/Thunderstorm, slower ❄ on Snow, a slow-rotating dashed amber halo on Clear — mapped defensively from `condition_code` (unknown codes animate nothing), decorative overlay only.
- **Product-level landing mockup** — the hero conversation demo now shows real live steps (staggered entrance, past step dims when the next lands, current one breathes twice then settles) and a transient 3-blink streaming caret on the Markdown reply; 1 new i18n key ×6 (`landing.chat_mockup.step_analyze`). Nested spans because two CSS animation classes on one element override each other (`animation` is a single shorthand property).
- **Animated milestone toast** — the relationship-milestone toast icon upgrades from static ✨ to the shared `AnimatedEmoji` (asset already self-hosted).

### Tests

- **+11 frontend tests** — mood-glow contract (active/inactive/gate-closed), cross-fade phase contract, and 6 particle-gating cases (whitelist, threshold, never-on-mount, history rows, reduced motion). Full suite green: 509 tests / 49 files, ESLint + `tsc --noEmit` clean, Prettier clean repo-wide on `src`, i18n parity ×6.

## [1.23.11] - 2026-07-11

> The structural-decoupling release (ADR-126). Audit cycle 3's coupling metrics exposed a textbook Stable Dependencies violation: **auth** — the most depended-upon domain of the backend (26 afferent domains) — itself depended on 14 domains and sat in 11 of the 31 bidirectional import cycles. Three behavior-preserving lots later, the boundary is clean: **auth = identity & sessions (a leaf: 2 outgoing edges, 0 incoming, 0 cycles); users = the User aggregate, profile and account lifecycle (the coherent hub)**. Zero behavior change by construction — no endpoint, wire contract, transaction topology or structlog event touched; the full backend suites ran green at every lot boundary and the `User` class moved byte-identically (proven by blob comparison against HEAD).

### Added

- **`scripts/audit/measure_coupling.py`** — the domain-coupling instrument (Ca/Ce/instability matrix + bidirectional-cycle list) is now committed, closing the audit-protocol "coupling measurement due" item. It reproduces the cycle-3 figures exactly (all-imports semantics, `TYPE_CHECKING` included) and adds runtime-only columns (`_rt`) — only runtime imports can produce circular-import failures, so the Stable Dependencies assessment reads those while the historical series stays comparable. `--detail <domain>` lists a domain's outgoing edges with exact `file:line` sites.
- **`users/AccountProvisioningService`** — the creation-side counterpart of `AccountDeletionService`: provisions skill activation states and default usage limits for new accounts (registration + OAuth creation). The two historical call sites had different transaction topologies (registration commits per step, the OAuth callback commits once at the end), preserved exactly via an explicit `commit_per_step` flag.
- **`src/core/geo_utils.py`** — `haversine_distance` promoted from the agents domain (pure math, no domain knowledge); the agents `distance` module keeps a compat alias, and the haversine test suite moved to `tests/unit/core/test_geo_utils.py`.
- **`get_provider_api_key()`** in `core/llm_config_helper.py` — core-level probe for provider API-key availability (used by the voice-mode STT capability check), replacing a direct domain import of the LLM-config cache.

### Changed

- **`User` ORM model moved from `auth/models.py` to `users/models.py`** (its historical re-export home) — byte-identical class body, ~84 import sites plus tests migrated mechanically, transitional shim deleted, model registration untouched (`import_all_models()`); no DB change of any kind (the `users` table never moved, no Alembic migration).
- **`user_location_service` moved from auth to users** (profile/location concern): the last-known-location cascade, its router endpoints' service and its unit tests now live in the users domain; the 4 external importers (agents chat geolocation, briefing weather, heartbeat proactive cascade, users home-deletion wipe) updated.
- **Account provisioning extracted out of `AuthService`** — `register()` and the OAuth user-creation path now delegate to `AccountProvisioningService`; existing auth unit tests pass unmodified (lazy imports preserved the source-level patch targets).
- Living docs updated to the new layout (`AUTHENTICATION.md`, `LAST_KNOWN_LOCATION` runbook, `GUIDE_TESTING.md`, audit protocol §6); historical ADRs left untouched (dated documents). New [ADR-126](docs/architecture/ADR-126-Auth-Users-Domain-Decoupling.md) documents the boundary, the measured before/after matrix and the accepted hub-cycle relocation trade-off.

### Fixed

- `auth/service.py` imported its own `User` model back through the users re-export (`auth → users → auth` indirection) — now imports it directly; the gratuitous `auth↔users` runtime cycle from that edge is gone.
- Dead borrowed-private-symbol import (`_haversine_distance` from agents internals) eliminated — the historical cross-domain private-helper case flagged by the audit.

### Metrics (measure_coupling.py, before → after)

- Ce(auth): **14 → 2** (users, shared) · runtime: **6 → 2** — target ≤3 met on the audit's own instrument.
- Ca(auth): **26 → 0** (sole remaining importer: `api/v1/routes.py`, outside the domain graph).
- Cycles involving auth: **11 → 0**. Hub pairs relocate to the users domain (raw totals 31→32 all-imports, 24→31 runtime-only: the former typing-only auth cycles re-form as honestly-runtime users↔X pairs — accidental hub → coherent lifecycle hub, the full trade-off is documented in ADR-126); no cycle outside the users hub was created.

### Tests

- +12 unit tests: `AccountProvisioningService` (5 — both commit topologies, feature-flag gate, default safety), `get_provider_api_key` (2), haversine suite relocated to core (13 moved, 1 constant test). Full suites green at every lot boundary (~9,265 unit / 140 integration / 969 agents on the final run set), MyPy strict 0 errors on 870 files, Docker boot verified per lot.

## [1.23.10] - 2026-07-11

> The living-interface release. LIA's frontend gains a coherent system of micro-interactions that makes the assistant feel alive without ever getting in the way: the Psyche Engine becomes _visible_ (the mood avatar is now a real animated face on the current reply, the ring pulses when the mood shifts, relationship milestones are celebrated), the pipeline's execution steps breathe while they run, and a dozen small touches (random typing-indicator shapes, streaming caret, animated personality emojis in the header, a living tab title for background runs) replace static chrome with motion that carries meaning. Everything is pure frontend polish behind hard fallbacks — every animation degrades to the previous behavior on asset failure, when psyche visuals are hidden, and under `prefers-reduced-motion` (where animated assets are not even fetched). No backend change, no DB migration, no new dependency, no new setting.
>
> **Asset note:** animations use Google's Noto Animated Emoji (CC BY 4.0), self-hosted under `apps/web/public/animated-emoji/` (23 WebP, ~10 MB, attribution LICENSE included). The original 512px encodes are shipped unmodified: a 128px Pillow re-encode was tried and reverted because it flattened the variable per-frame timings and made the animations visibly choppy.

### Added

- **`AnimatedEmoji` shared component** (`components/ui/animated-emoji.tsx`) — renders a self-hosted animated Noto WebP for any emoji glyph with three hermetic fallbacks: static glyph when animation is not requested, per-codepoint error memory on missing/corrupt assets, and no render (no fetch) under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Codepoints are derived at runtime from the glyph itself (variation selectors included, e.g. ⚖️ → `2696-fe0f`), so DB-managed emojis need no frontend registry.
- **Animated psyche avatar** — the mood smiley on the **latest assistant message only** is a live animated face; older messages keep their static mood snapshots (at most one permanent loop on screen) but **wake up while hovered**. Mood→codepoint mapping lives in `MOOD_COLORS` with an asset-completeness test (ADR-085 spirit: every mood must have its WebP on disk).
- **Animated personality emojis (header)** — the current personality's emoji lives permanently in the header trigger; menu items animate on hover/focus only (one loop at a time, assets fetched on demand). Best-effort by design: the 4 seeded emojis without a Noto animated version (🌴 ⚛️ 🥟 💰) keep their static glyph, silently.
- **Typing indicator variants** — 6 pure-CSS animations (wave, orbit, equalizer, sparkle ✦, breathe, typewriter), one picked at random per response; classic gray tint kept; static three dots under reduced motion (never a frozen shape).
- **Live execution steps** — the progress lines ("📋 Preparing the action plan…") now have a visual hierarchy: past steps dim to 55 %, the current one slides in and breathes until the next arrives. Built on a new typed `streaming.phase` (`'progress' | 'answer'`) field in the chat reducer FSM, threaded through every SSE handler dispatch.
- **Streaming caret** — a blinking caret marks the end of the text while answer tokens stream (answer phase only; hidden under reduced motion).
- **Living tab title** — while a run streams and the tab is hidden, the title alternates with "✦ LIA is writing…" (6 languages) and restores exactly on done/visibility/unmount — the visible companion of ADR-117 background runs.
- **Psyche made perceptible** — one-shot **mood-ring ping** (scale + brightness) when the live avatar's mood changes between replies; **relationship milestone toasts** (headless `PsycheMilestoneWatcher`: forward-only ORIENTATION → EXPLORATORY → AFFECTIVE → STABLE transitions, hydration-guarded so a page load never toasts, 6 languages).
- **Micro-touches** — send-button takeoff on submit, slow glimmer on the active skill badge ✦, animated 👋 greeting on the empty chat, hover-animated mood emoji on the settings psyche card.
- **`scripts/assets/fetch_noto_animated_emoji.py`** — one-shot fetcher for all animated assets: strict on the 14 mood codepoints (exit 1 on a missing one), best-effort on personality/UI emojis (`MISS` report, static glyph at runtime).

### Changed

- **`AssistantAvatar` refactored onto the shared `AnimatedEmoji`** (its inline img/fallback logic removed); `TypingIndicator` rewritten around the variant table; `ChatMessageList` computes the last assistant message id (`getLastAssistantMessageId`) to gate the single live animation.
- **Reduced-motion coverage extended** — the project's kill-switch is an explicit class list, not a wildcard: every new animation class is registered there, and the typing indicator swaps to static dots via `motion-reduce:` DOM classes rather than freezing mid-shape.

## [1.23.5] - 2026-07-10

> Security-hygiene release: production maintenance stops handling credentials, and the repository stops shipping real server coordinates. The post-deploy reindex runbook (`scripts/prod-reindex-gemini.sh`) instructed the operator to paste a **superuser session cookie** into a `curl` command run over SSH on the prod box — a replayable admin bearer token that lands in `~/.bash_history` (and its backups), defeating the `HttpOnly` flag the cookie is deliberately set with, even though the same script already held root-level `docker exec` access three steps above. RAG Spaces reindexation now runs fully in-container through a new CLI, consistent with the sibling embedding reindex. In the same pass, the real production SSH coordinates (host, port, username) were scrubbed from five tracked files and aligned to the repo's existing `<user>@<prod-host>` placeholder convention.

### Security

- **Reindex runbook no longer transmits a session cookie** — `scripts/prod-reindex-gemini.sh` step 5 printed a `curl -X POST /rag-spaces/admin/reindex -H "Cookie: session_id=…"` instruction, training the operator to exfiltrate an `HttpOnly` superuser cookie from the browser into shell history on the production host — a full-admin bearer token, replayable and long-lived, with only `SameSite=Lax` as CSRF defense. It is replaced by an in-container `docker exec … python scripts/reindex_rag_spaces.py` call: no HTTP round-trip, no cookie, consistent with steps 2-4 which already reindex via `docker exec` (the operator is already root-equivalent inside the box). (CWE-522 / CWE-532 / CWE-214.)
- **Real production SSH coordinates scrubbed from tracked files** — the real production host, SSH port and username appeared verbatim in five tracked files (the reindex script header, the `PublicEndpointDown` and `COMPACTION_v2` runbooks, a DevOps SSH test fixture, and a historical CHANGELOG note). They are aligned to the `<user>@<prod-host>` placeholder convention already used by `infrastructure/README.md` and `docker-compose.prod.yml`; the test fixture moves to RFC-5737 documentation values (`192.0.2.10`). Recon-only exposure (an RFC-1918 address behind the Cloudflare tunnel, LAN port refused externally), removed for hygiene. (CWE-200.)

### Added

- **`scripts/reindex_rag_spaces.py`** — CLI companion to `reindex_embeddings.py` that re-embeds every user RAG document with the currently configured model, in-container, to completion. It is the operational equivalent of `POST /rag-spaces/admin/reindex` without the HTTP layer or a session cookie; loads provider API keys from the DB (as the sibling script does) before embedding.
- **`run_in_background` flag on `start_reindexation`** — HTTP callers keep the detached fire-and-forget behaviour (default `True`); the CLI passes `False` so the process awaits `_reindex_all_documents` instead of exiting and killing the work mid-flight. Single source of truth for the setup/guard logic (Redis mutex, dimension `ALTER`, singleton reset) — no duplication.

### Tests

- 2 unit tests on the `run_in_background` branch: `False` awaits the reindex to completion and never detaches it; `True` (default) detaches via `safe_fire_and_forget` and never awaits inline. First direct coverage of `start_reindexation`. The DevOps SSH service fixture change is behaviour-neutral (assertions pin command structure, not the coordinates).

## [1.23.4] - 2026-07-10

> Hardening release closing the last gap in the tool protection policy. A full inventory of the 47 tool modules found that the image generation tools — among the most expensive per-call paid APIs in the catalogue — were the **only** family carrying neither `@track_tool_metrics` nor `@rate_limit`, with no client-layer limiter either (`ImageGenerationClient` is a standalone ABC, unlike Perplexity/Brave whose connector clients embed a Redis rate limiter). Their only guards were the usage-limits cost caps — per billing cycle and Redis-cached (~30 s TTL), so a runaway ReAct loop or a prompt-injection burst could overshoot them before they bite. Both tools now carry the full standard decorator stack, and the DevOps Claude CLI tool (a paid Claude run **plus** real actions on a remote server over SSH) gains its own per-user ceiling. Every threshold is settings-driven — tunable in production without rebuild.

### Added

- **Rate limiting + standard metrics on image generation** — `generate_image` and `edit_image` now carry `@track_tool_metrics` (`agent_tool_invocations` / `agent_tool_duration_seconds` under `image_generation_agent`) and a settings-driven per-user `@rate_limit` (sliding window, default **10 calls / 5 min**, tracked separately per tool). Exceeding the threshold short-circuits the tool **before** the paid API call with the standard `rate_limit_exceeded` payload (`retry_after_seconds` included) and increments `agent_tool_rate_limit_hits_total`. New settings: `IMAGE_GENERATION_RATE_LIMIT_CALLS` / `IMAGE_GENERATION_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW`.
- **Rate limiting on the DevOps Claude CLI tool** — `claude_server_task_tool` (already metric-tracked, admin-only) gains a per-user `@rate_limit` (default **5 calls / 10 min**): each call is a paid Claude CLI run plus real SSH actions on a server; admin-only reduces exposure but not runaway risk, and each task lasts up to ~120 s wall-clock so the ceiling cannot hinder normal sequential admin use. New settings: `DEVOPS_RATE_LIMIT_CALLS` / `DEVOPS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW`.

### Fixed

- **Image generation was outside the tool protection policy** — the systemic rule "every tool carries `@track_tool_metrics` AND `@rate_limit`, especially tools hitting paid external APIs" cited image generation by name, yet the module had neither decorator and no protection at any other layer. Both execution paths are covered: the parallel executor injects the `ToolRuntime` the limiter keys on before its direct coroutine calls, and the ReAct loop gets it via standard LangChain injection.

### Tests

- 11 new unit tests (no DB, no network): threshold exceedance returns the standard `rate_limit_exceeded` payload anchored on `ToolErrorCode.RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` for all three tools, `generate_image` / `edit_image` have independent per-tool sliding windows, the Prometheus hit counter fires exactly once per block, and thresholds are read from settings at call time (never hardcoded). Registry smoke green (96 tools); full fast suite **9,082 passed**.

## [1.23.3] - 2026-07-10

> The semantic layer becomes deterministic and fully wired, and every request gets faster. Three worksites land together. **Latency**: the router's semantic pivot now runs in parallel with memory resolution (**−1.1s p50 on the first token of every graph turn**, measured n=5), the response-context bundle is prefetched at router entry, and a new per-stage duration histogram makes the whole graph measurable in production. **Semantic reliability** ([ADR-120](docs/architecture/ADR-120-Semantic-Evidence-Expansion-And-Param-Guard.md), [ADR-121](docs/architecture/ADR-121-Semantic-Annotation-Backfill.md)): the recurring "route to my brother" failure — the plan sometimes geocoded the person's _name_ to a random location and cached the wrong route — is closed at three levels (deterministic person-reference evidence, a manifest-driven runtime guard in both execution modes, and an unresolvable-destination error in `get_route`), and the audit it triggered revealed that **73 of the 99 ontology types were consumed by no tool manifest**: ~130 annotations later, cross-domain chains like "email the attendees of this meeting" or "reply to the sender" are finally expressible. **Background-run robustness** (ADR-117 follow-up): a hard-killed producer (kill -9, OOM, power loss) can no longer leak TTL-less Redis keys nor leave subscribers waiting forever — orphaned streams now end with a clear, localized error. The measurement protocol behind the latency numbers ships in the repo (`scripts/perf/measure_ttft.py` + [docs/optim/LATENCY_PLAN.md](docs/optim/LATENCY_PLAN.md)).

### Added

- **Runtime semantic parameter guard ([ADR-120](docs/architecture/ADR-120-Semantic-Evidence-Expansion-And-Param-Guard.md))** — `semantic/param_guard.py`, manifest-driven, zero per-tool hardcode: a tool argument that is _exactly_ a person name resolved this turn on a parameter typed `physical_address`/`email_address` fails fast with a recoverable error BEFORE the paid API call, in both execution modes (parallel executor via `configurable.resolved_person_names` — sourced from state, the only conduit that survives a HITL resume — and the ReAct execute-tools node, before the HITL interrupt so users are never asked to approve a doomed call). Fail-open by design; metric `semantic_param_guard_blocks_total{tool_name,semantic_type,execution_mode}`.
- **Evidence-driven domain expansion under flag ([ADR-120](docs/architecture/ADR-120-Semantic-Evidence-Expansion-And-Param-Guard.md))** — `SEMANTIC_EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_DRIVEN_ENABLED` (ships dark): every referenced entity (person → `Contact`, previously-shown event/place/email → `CalendarEvent`/`Place`/`EmailMessage`) whose ontology `properties` provide a semantic type required by the selected domains' tools adds its provider domains to the planner catalogue — capped (`SEMANTIC_EXPANSION_MAX_ADDED_DOMAINS`), counted (`semantic_expansion_total{evidence_entity,added_domain}`), and anchored on the entity so "quel temps demain ?" never expands blindly. The evidence→entity mapping is completeness-asserted at boot (ADR-085 pattern). For person-only evidence the outcome is identical to the always-on historical path, keeping the future flag flip low-risk.
- **Semantic annotation back-fill ([ADR-121](docs/architecture/ADR-121-Semantic-Annotation-Backfill.md))** — an exhaustive inventory of the live catalogue (75 tools) found **31/224 parameters (14%) and 75/336 outputs (22%) semantically typed, with 73/99 ontology types consumed by no manifest**. ~130 one-line annotations across 15 manifest files later: **120/224 params (53%), 137/338 outputs (40%), 72/100 types consumed**. Flagship chains pinned by tests on the real manifests: event attendees → `send_email.to`, email sender → `create_event.attendees`, `route.destination` → weather/places location, place address → contact address. Campaign rule: no output annotated without verifying the path against the real tool payload (Jinja references execute on it) — which is how `emails[].from` was found NOT to exist (Gmail buries the sender in `payload.headers[]`, unaddressable): it is now promoted top-level in `build_emails_output`, mirroring the existing `subject` promotion.
- **`EmailMessage` ontology entity** — `properties = {sender: email_address, thread: thread_id, identifier: message_id}`: a referenced email becomes expansion evidence ("invite the sender of this email to the meeting").
- **Per-stage graph duration instrumentation** — `langgraph_stage_duration_seconds{stage,execution_mode,turn_kind}` histogram observed at the SSE chokepoint (buffered, flushed at turn end and HITL interrupts) plus a per-turn `graph_stage_durations` structured log (Loki-queryable where multiprocess Prometheus is unavailable); `agent_node_duration_seconds` extended to router/planner/ReAct nodes; TTFT/streaming/router/validator histogram buckets recalibrated to production (RPi5) scales.
- **Reproducible TTFT measurement protocol** — `scripts/perf/measure_ttft.py` (13 scenarios × pipeline/ReAct, cache-busting variants, HITL seed turns, per-stage and per-LLM-site `/metrics` deltas) and [docs/optim/LATENCY_PLAN.md](docs/optim/LATENCY_PLAN.md) (systemic baseline, stage×path matrix, decision log with before/after for every optimization).
- **Orphaned-run exit for background streams** (ADR-117 hard-kill follow-up) — the SSE relay now probes the conversation's heartbeated active-run lock during chunk silence: lock missing (or owned by another stream) for a full grace period → synthetic, localized `error` + `done{error, orphaned}` chunks instead of an infinite wait. The heartbeated lock is the liveness source of truth (a long LLM call is silent but alive), a probe failure is never treated as a missing lock, and `BACKGROUND_RUNS_ORPHAN_GRACE_SECONDS` is boot-validated ≥ 2× the producer heartbeat. Worst-case exit after a crash ≈ 70s in production.

### Changed

- **Router: semantic pivot ∥ memory resolution (latency R1)** — the English-pivot LLM call now overlaps the memory-resolution phase inside `analyze_full` (the phases are data-independent: memory embeds the original-language query). **Router stage −1.1s p50, 100% of graph turns**, both modes, zero behavioural drift (n=5 × 13 scenarios, 0 errors). The pivot task is cancelled best-effort if analysis fails first.
- **Response-context prefetch at router entry (latency R2)** — the response node's context bundle (personality, memory, TTS…) starts loading when the router starts instead of when the response node is reached (flag `RESPONSE_CONTEXT_PREFETCH_AT_ROUTER_ENABLED`, default on); the system-RAG part stays deferred to the response node because app-help detection doesn't exist yet at router time (`ResponseContextBundle.system_rag_deferred`). −0.1/−0.3s pre-first-token on conversational/ReAct turns in dev; larger expected in production.
- **Semantic pivot behind a flag (latency R3)** — `SEMANTIC_PIVOT_ENABLED` (default on, no behaviour change): the A/B run (135 vs 117 FR turns) showed zero intent/domain/route drift with the pivot off and ~zero latency delta post-R1 (the memory branch dominates) — the flag turns a future "−1 LLM call per turn" cost decision into a one-line flip once a broader corpus is validated.
- **Person-reference evidence made deterministic ([ADR-120](docs/architecture/ADR-120-Semantic-Evidence-Expansion-And-Param-Guard.md))** — the semantic-expansion trigger `has_person_reference` is now the union of three sources (memory-resolver mappings — person references by construction; Phase-1 extracted relational references, preserved even when resolution finds no memory fact via the new typed `MemoryResolution` result; analyzer-LLM person refs — the historical, intermittent signal that was previously the ONLY one consulted, in contradiction with the expansion service's documented contract). Evidence sources are logged and surfaced in the debug panel. One corrected domain list feeds the planner catalogue, the planner prompt's semantic-dependencies section AND the ReAct system prompt — the fix serves both modes.
- **Stream safety TTL from the first chunk** (ADR-117 hard-kill follow-up) — every chunk `XADD` now pipelines an `EXPIRE NX` in the same round-trip: the stream key carries a bounded safety TTL (`BACKGROUND_RUNS_STREAM_SAFETY_TTL_SECONDS`, boot-validated ≥ stream TTL) from its very first entry, self-re-arming, while `publish_end` keeps overwriting it with the short post-terminal TTL. A producer dying without its terminal marker can no longer leak a TTL-less key through the Redis AOF.

### Fixed

- **"Route to my brother" intermittently geocoding the person's name** — the exact failure chain (memory resolved the person but the analyzer omitted the person typing → no contact expansion → `get_route(destination="<person name>")` → arbitrary geocode → wrong route **cached 300s**) is closed at all three levels: deterministic evidence (above), the runtime guard (above), and `get_route` now returning a recoverable `destination_unresolved` error when a non-address destination that Places cannot find would otherwise be passed raw to the Routes API — nothing is cached on that path, and the error message steers the model to fetch the real address first. A Places _API failure_ still passes through (an outage is not evidence the destination is bad).
- **Listener counter crash window** (ADR-117 hard-kill follow-up) — `INCR` and `EXPIRE` ran as two separate Redis calls; a crash between them produced a TTL-less counter stuck >0, wrongly triggering paid voice synthesis for absent listeners forever. The increment is now a single Lua `EVAL` (symmetric with the existing decrement), which also saves a round-trip.
- **PII at INFO level** — resolved person-name mappings were logged in clear at INFO in the query analyzer; now counts at INFO, contents at DEBUG.
- **Semantic-linking tests ran against an empty registry** — the `agent_registry` fixture's docstring claimed manifests "auto-load"; they never did, so every historical Jinja2-suggestion test silently exercised the not-found path. The fixture now calls `initialize_catalogue()` and the new flagship-chain tests pin real suggestions on real manifests.
- **Dead code removed** — the never-wired `expand_domains_semantic` (threshold-based expansion) and its orphan setting `SEMANTIC_EXPANSION_THRESHOLD` (defined, read by nobody) are deleted, superseded by evidence-driven expansion; stale plural-vocabulary docstrings in the semantic module corrected to the singular domain registry; `TERMINAL_STATUSES` in the stream broker now includes `cancelled` (the tuple was documentation that lied).

### Tests

- **+52 tests** (suite at **9,093 passed**): person-evidence gate (E1/E2/E3 sources, entity mapping), runtime param guard (exact-match, list params, fail-open paths, config plumbing), `get_route` destination guard (marker + tool conversion + passthrough cases), evidence-driven expansion (entity anchoring, cap determinism, per-entity cases, boot-assert refusal), semantic-pivot overlap (R1 contract: memory gets the original query, analyzer the awaited translation, no orphaned task), system-RAG deferral, flagship semantic chains on real manifests, and an integration test for the orphaned-stream exit.

## [1.23.2] - 2026-07-10

> The alerting chain comes back to life ([ADR-119](docs/architecture/ADR-119-Alerting-Reactivation-Minimal-Core.md)). Alerting had been silently disabled since 2026-01-16 — ~71 maintained rules and 22 runbooks were dormant, nobody was notified of any incident (the only signal was the daily logwatch digest), and DORA MTTR was unmeasurable. This release ships a minimal viable core of **13 vital alerts** evaluated by Prometheus and delivered by **email** through a dedicated Alertmanager in production, proven end-to-end in dev (Redis stopped → `[CRITICAL]` email in the inbox in 3m30 → restart → `resolved` email). The audit that preceded the reactivation found the legacy thresholds **corrupted** (blind ×1.5/×3/×7.5 multipliers on bounded percentages — production disk alert at 147% usage, literally unfireable), which is why the core is a fresh, unit-tested rule set rather than a blanket re-enable.

### Added

- **13-alert core (`alerts-core.yml`)** — ServiceDown, DatabaseDown (`up` OR `pg_up`), RedisDown, DiskSpaceCritical, ContainerMemoryNearLimit, ContainerRestartLoop, HighErrorRate (with a **minimum-traffic guard** so low-volume periods can't fire 100%-of-2-requests noise), SSELatencyP95High (threshold set above the measured production TTFT baseline to catch degradation, not enforce an aspirational SLA), BackupFailed, PublicEndpointDown, CertificateExpirySoon, plus two meta-alerts (AlertmanagerDown, ObservabilityScrapeTargetMissing). Every alert annotates its runbook; thresholds are `ALERT_CORE_*` variables in `thresholds/{env}.env` rendered by the existing `prepare_config.sh` pipeline, and **descriptions reference the same template variables as expressions** — the displayed threshold can never drift from the firing threshold again.
- **Alertmanager in production** (`docker-compose.prod.yml`, 128M/0.25 cpu — RPi5-scale like the other sidecars): the pre-existing entrypoint renders the config from `ALERTMANAGER_*` env vars and auto-selects the **email-only** template when Slack/PagerDuty are unset; missing SMTP degrades to log-only instead of crashing. Grafana unified alerting deliberately stays unused (no `promtool test rules` equivalent, evaluation load on a tightly-sized Grafana, silent single point of failure).
- **blackbox-exporter** (64M/0.1 cpu, both compose files) probing what no existing exporter saw: the postgres-backup sidecar's healthcheck webhook (`BackupFailed` — ADR-109 restore capability at risk) and the public URL end-to-end through Cloudflare edge → cloudflared tunnel → web (`PublicEndpointDown`, `CertificateExpirySoon`). The public target is injected at Prometheus startup from `BLACKBOX_PUBLIC_PROBE_URL` (.env) into a file_sd file — the real domain never lands in the open-source repo; empty variable = probe disabled (dev default).
- **17 promtool unit tests** (`prometheus/tests/alerts_core_test.yml`) — 13 firing cases + 4 negative cases (disk below threshold, healthy Redis, the HighErrorRate traffic guard) asserting labels **and rendered annotations**, so the threshold values displayed in notifications are pinned to the expression values by CI-runnable tests.
- **4 new runbooks** — [RedisDown](docs/runbooks/alerts/RedisDown.md), [BackupFailed](docs/runbooks/alerts/BackupFailed.md), [PublicEndpointDown](docs/runbooks/alerts/PublicEndpointDown.md) (covers the recurring cloudflared-tunnel incident profile), [AlertmanagerDown](docs/runbooks/alerts/AlertmanagerDown.md) (the meta-alert that cannot email you by definition — assumed limitation documented, external dead-man's-switch listed as future hardening).

### Changed

- **Alertmanager configuration consolidated** under `infrastructure/observability/alertmanager/` — it lived in `apps/api/monitoring/` (mounted by dev) with a divergent orphaned copy under `prometheus/alertmanager/`; infra config does not belong to the API app. Line endings normalized to LF (the entrypoint is a POSIX sh script executed in-container). Never-loaded custom alert files regrouped under `infrastructure/observability/prometheus/alerts/`.
- **`prepare_config.sh`** now renders `alerts-core.yml` first (the only file Prometheus loads), labels the legacy renders as NOT loaded, and prefers the repo venv's Python (system python lacking jinja2/pyyaml made the script unusable on dev machines).
- **Alerting docs consolidated**: new canonical [README_ALERTING.md](docs/readme/README_ALERTING.md) (architecture, entrypoint mode-selection table, SMTP provider notes, routing/inhibitions, the 5 validation commands, troubleshooting — including the "Gmail filter moves alerts out of INBOX" trap observed during the E2E test); `README_ALERT_MANAGER2.md`, `README_PROMETHEUS_ALERTMANAGER.md` and `README_ALERTING_SMTP.md` (~3,575 lines describing dead mechanisms or duplicating legacy YAML) deleted; [README_PROMETHEUS_THRESHOLDS.md](docs/readme/README_PROMETHEUS_THRESHOLDS.md) rewritten around the live pipeline and the legacy-threshold corruption.
- **`.env` surfaces**: `BLACKBOX_PUBLIC_PROBE_URL` added to `.env.example` / `.env.prod.example`; `.env.min.prod` gains the minimal `[11] ALERTING` section (SMTP + recipient + probe URL) — the alerting chain is configurable from the minimal deployment file.

### Fixed

- **Legacy alert thresholds proven corrupted and quarantined** — the 2025-11 threshold generator applied blind environment multipliers (production ×1.5, staging ×3, development ×7.5) to bounded percentages: `DiskSpaceCritical` at **147%** disk usage in production (294% staging, 735% dev), CPU/memory at 142.5%, error rate at 30% instead of the documented 5%. Even if re-enabled, disk/CPU/memory/5xx alerting could never have fired. The legacy files stay unloaded with recalibration mandated before any group returns to `rule_files`; threshold-file headers now state it and `README_PROMETHEUS_THRESHOLDS.md` documents the corruption table.
- **Even the dev Alertmanager was a zombie** — the container ran but Prometheus neither loaded any alert rule nor targeted it (the shared `prometheus.yml` had the `alerting:` block commented out); dev now exercises the same chain as production, which is how the E2E proof was run.
- **Housekeeping of the living config directory** — 22 one-shot migration scripts, `.original/.production/.rendered` archives and analysis dumps deleted from `infrastructure/observability/prometheus/` (zero references outside historical docs, recoverable from git history); 126 lines of dead code (`THRESHOLD_MAPPING`) removed from `render_alerts.py`; legacy rendered rule files resynchronized with their templates.

The landing proof band, README, FAQ, /story pages, SEO descriptions and knowledge base all point to it, and every published audit figure was refreshed from the stale 8.0/20-areas to 8.4/24 in the same sweep.

- **Reproducible audit protocol — [docs/audit/AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md](docs/audit/AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md)**: 7 non-negotiable invariants (commit pinning, evidence-only findings, counter-verification, executed suites, logical-SLOC metrics, register continuity, inline conduct), per-area minimum evidence sets for all 24 areas, anchored scoring discipline, and the 7-step constants-first publication pipeline — a future audit cycle is triggered by a single request and lands on every public surface. `CLAUDE.md` documentation pointers reference it.

Standard library only.
